 through enhanced availability of identified planting stock with desired traits.  The Committee was informed that the Task
 Force on Plant Material provided by Department of Biotechnology on plant tissue culture (Introduction plant) Tissue
 Culture set up by the Department of Biotechnology considered the need for initiating specific programmes for different
 plant species.  Thus, a number of research and development projects were supported for perfecting complete protocols of
 important plant species – Forest Trees, Horticulture Crops and Plantation Crops.  The  objective behind these  projects was
 to develop a package of technology for production of large quantities of planting material of improved varieties.  Two
 Tissue Culture Pilot Plant facilities were also set up for large-scale production of elite planting material with the main
 objective of demonstrating the field performance of tissue culture raised plants forest trees. 
13.The Committee was informed that plant tissue culture technology has been commercialised and many companies in India
 were producing large quantities of planting materials.  Commercialisation of technology requires scaling up and field
 evaluation before transfer to the industry.  The Department of Biotechnology supported projects have successfully
 standardised complete protocols and processes for a number of economically viable  plant species.  These protocols have
 been scaled up at the Hardening Units and tissue Culture Pilot Plants.  The Tissue Culture Pilot Plants were converted to
 Micropropagation Technology Parks (MTP) to provide an effective platform for transfer of the proven technologies to the
 entrepreneurs.  The MTP’s at National Chemical Laboratory, Pune & Tata Energy Research Institute, New Delhi have
 optimised a large number of technologies and also transferred to the industry.
14.The Committee feels that with a view to replenish  the depleting forest cover and improve the environment  the role of
 tissue culture technique  has assumpted importance.  The committee observes that the techniques if proved successful in
 case of ongoing projects, may be replicated in  case of value based forest trees, horticultural crops and plantation crops.
MEDICAL BIOTECHNOLOGY
15.In the area of medical biotechnology, the Department proposes to lay  emphasis on the development of diagnostics,
 vaccines for prophylactic and therapeutic use, drug delivery systems, production of important biological/biomolecules and
 creation of infrastructures in hitech biomedical areas in order to undertake further research.  During the year 1999-2000 the
 Department  has considered 42 new projects besides monitoring 55 ongoing projects and the National Jai Vigyan
 
Science and Technology Mission on development of New Generation technologies for Vaccines were initiated..
16.The department has been funding research for the development of indigenous diagnostics for major communicable and
 non-communicable diseases.  The basic purpose has been to develop easy to use, affordable and accurate test systems for
 Indian strains which could be converted into appropriate kits with the help of industries for large scale use.  The Committee
 was informed that after reaching  the level of prototype systems, the department is endeavouring  to upscale these
 technologies. The Committee was apprised of the achievements made in the area of major communicable and non-
communicable diseases which include HIV/AIDS, Japanese Encepalitis, Hepatitis, Tuberculosis, Cholera, Shipella, 
 Rotavirus,  Helicobacter pylori, Leishmaniasis Malaria etc
17.The Committee recommends that besides supporting and developing indigenous diagnostics for major communicable and
 non-communicable diseases, the department should simultaneously endeavour to find market for indigenous products, and
 strive for better qualities to ensure priority for indigenous products over the imported ones.
HUMAN GENETICS AND GENOME ANALYSIS
18.The “Human Genetics & Genome Analysis” programme was initiated during 1994 with the objective to identify, map
 and characterise genes related to genetic disorders prevalent in India for diagnosis, prevention and management of genetic
 disorders and to develop new methods of the analysis and interpretations of genomic DNA sequences. Genetic diagnosis-
cum-counselling units established by the department have been providing molecular diagnosis and counselling for the
 common genetic disorders such as betathalassemia, Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), haemoglobinopathies and
 neurogenetic disorders prevalent in the country, to the affected families.
19.The Committee was informed that since the inception of 14 genetic diagnosis cum counselling units, about 11,000
 affected families have benefitted from prenatal diagnosis and counselling for major genetic disorders an a population of
 1,700 tribals screened for these disorders.
20.While the Committee commends the efforts made by the Department in providing counselling and diagnostics services
 for the common genetic disorders prevalent in the country to the affected families, the question remains how many people
 are aware of such facilities.  Such programmes and facilities should be named in a language which people can understand. 
 The symptoms of such disorders should be publicised as also the programmes and facilities.   The Committee therefore
 recommends that the Department may provide wide publicity to the programme by involving print as well as electronic
 media so that the benefits of these activities of the Department could percolate to the underprivileged and weaker sections
 of the society.
FOOD BIOTECHNOLOGY
21.The  Committee  has  been  given  to  understand  that  efforts  are  underway   for commissioning of pilot plants for

 large-scale production of low cost nutrient food supplements developed through biotechnological processes.  Several leads
 were obtained for rapid diagnosis of various food-borne pathogens like Salmonella sp., Bacillus cereus, Shigella sp. and
 Rotavirus. A lead has been obtained for prevention of Rotavirus diarrhoea in children below two years of age, by use of

22.The Committee notes with satisfaction the achievements made by the Department in the field of food Biotechnology. 
 The Committee however feels, that much more efforts are needed in the field to create awareness about the progarmme.
BIOTECHNOLOGY BASED PROGRAMMES FOR SOCIETY
23.DBT has started a new scheme, for the  last two years, for the empowerment and skill development of women and rural
 poor for their economic upliftment.  The Department is extending support in the areas of food technology, sericulture,
 floriculture, organic farming, waste management, medicinal plants, biodiversity conservation, aquaculture, environment
 protection and awareness building.  This programme has benefitted more than 6000 women including rural poor.
24.The  Committee  notes  with satisfaction the efforts made by the Department for upliftment of SC/ST population of
 country, women and rural poor. The Department has launched Biotechnology based programme  for the welfare of SC/ST
 population through proven technologies.  It facilitates SC/ST population to upgrade their skills and create additional job
 avenues or help in improving their health status.  The main activities are cultivation and distillation of medicinal and
 aromatic plants, vermicomposting, spirulina production, fish and poultry farming, production and application of various
 biofertilisers for better soil health, biological control agents for plant pests and survey of genetic disorders and counseling. 
 Forty-three projects have been pursued in 19 states and union territories, which benefited about 15,000 families.  The
 Committee observes that benefits of such programmes should be equally distributed among all the intended sections of the
 society.
NATIONAL JAI VIGYAN MISSION ON DEVELOPMENT OF NEW GENERATION VACCINES
25.The Committee was informed that the Department has initiated the programme based on several leads obtained from the
 R&D projects funded by the department earlier.  The objectives of the programme include generating candidate vaccine(s)
 for diseases like cholera, rabies, Japanese encephalitis, tuberculosis, malaria and HIV.  The programme has been grouped
 under three categories.  Category (A) includes those ‘candidate vaccines’ where potential research leads are available and
 which now require clinical trials or generating pre-clinical data.  Under this category, vaccines for cholera and rabies are
 being attempted.  The programmes under category (B) are related to available leads on candidate vaccines where efficacy
 and immunogenicity need to be worked out.  The target vaccines are tissue culture-based Japanese encephalitis, DNA
 vaccines, epitope vaccinogenes of Japanese encephalitis and synthetic candidate malaria vaccine.  Under category (C),
 programmes requiring sustained R&D efforts with the possibility for development of candidate vaccine(s).  Under this
 category, efforts would be made to produce candidate prophylactic anti-HIV and DNA vaccines for tuberculosis.  It is
 expected that at the end of the programme at least 2-3 vaccines will be available for upscaling and use to control/contain the
 infections while others would reach the stage of the clinical trials.
26.As regards the activities of the vaccine production unit, namely, Bharat Immunologicals & Biologicals Coprn. Ltd.
 (BIBCOL) set up by the Department for the production of viral vaccines, the Committee was informed that BIBCOL is
 formulating Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) from imported bulk since January 1996 and is supplying it to the National
 Immunisation Programme.  During the year, the company has formulated 175 million doses of OPV, a part of which was
 supplied to UNICEF.  When enquired about the proposed diversification plan for production of BCG, Measles and Tetanus
 toxoid vaccines as submitted by BIBCOL, the Committee was informed that the proposed plan has been finalised from
 BIBCOL side and the same is being submitted to the operating agency namely BIFR.
 
 
BIOTECHNOLOGY INFORMATION SYSTEM
27.The Secretary, Department of Biotechnology informed the Committee that recognising the importance of the information
 technology for pursuing advanced research in modern biology and biotechnology, a bioinformatics programme, envisaged
 as a distributed database and network organisation, was launched during 1986-87.  The programme has become  very
 successful vehicle for transfer and exchange of knowledge, information, technology packages and references in the country
 involving 8-10 thousand scientists.  Ten Distributed Information Centres and 38 Sub-Distributed Information Centres
 located in universities and research institutions are fully engaged in this task, five national facilities have been set up for
 interactive graphics based molecular modeling and other biocomputational needs.  The entire network has emerged as a
 very sophisticated scientific infrastructure for bioinformatics involving state-of-the art computational and communication
 facilities.  The computer communication network, linking all the bioinformatics centres, is playing a vital role in the success
 of the bioinformatics programme.  Database development, R&D activities in bioinformatics, human resource development

 useful to the scientific community.
28.The Committee was apprised of the broad functions and services rendered by the Bioinformatics Centre which are as
 follows;-
(i)         the principal objectives of a Bioinformatics Centre is to function as an information base in each speciality so
 that the scientists have ready access to the computer-based information on resources, databases in subject
 fields, and to build up expertise in bioinformatics in keeping with the rapid development in this area;
(ii)        to provide a computer-based information storage and retrieval system of database that collects structured
 information generated by research and industrial institutions in the identified fields of biotechnology,
 continually update the databank and make the information available to the users;
(iii)       an active network mode, in which the scientists get access to the biotechnology community in the identified
 areas, answer requests for information in an interactive and discussive  mode and actively initiate dialogue
 among groups with common interest;
(iv)       to provide  retrieval service either online or offline in their specialised areas and to give overall information
 support even in areas other than those assigned to them;
(v)        to provide communication link with international databases for selective bibliographic information for the
 user scientists;
(vi)            to develop software packages and databases specific to user needs; and
(vii)      to conduct training courses in the specialised areas, periodically to meet the special requirements of
 manpower development in the area and to promote awareness about the computerised storage and retrieval
 facility among bio-scientists and information scientists.
29.The Committee commends the efforts made by the Department of Biotechnology in the field of bioinformatics, which are
 expected to yield multidimensional results in variety of areas.  The Committee, however, recommends that the Department
 should make all out efforts to ensure that biological data created in agricultural and other sectors be disseminated in a way
 
that it also reaches the persons working at grassroots levels and desiring to make use of it, so as to ensure optimum use of
 the data created
AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTIONS
30.Department of Biotechnology supports research activities in the autonomous institutions; viz; National Brain Research
 Centre, National Centre for Plant Genome Research, National Institute of Immunology, National Centre for Cell Science
 and Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics.
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF IMMUNOLOGY
31.The Committee was informed that the Institute has excelled in the pursuit of rigorous fundamental research and emerged
 as a centre of excellence in basic immunology, infectious diseases and molecular design.  As regards the most recent
 achievements of the Institute, the Committee was informed that a major fundamental discovery concerning pathogenesis,
 which concerns survival of bacteria in phagocytes, has been reported in the Journal of Cell Biology. The complete genome
 of an Indian isolate of JEV(GP78) has been sequenced revealing its evolutionary closeness to the Chinese SA14 isolate.  A
 novel immunomodulatory use of an Indian medicinal plant product (NII-60) to prevent septic shock received a US patent
 and was transferred to an Indian Pharmaceutical industry for commercialisation.  A transgenic mice expressing the hepatitis
 B virus X  gene has been generated.  In a novel strategy, genes for different stages of plasmodium falciparum have been
 stitched and expressed in baculovirus system.  The resultant proteins elicit good immune response in experimental animals.
32.The allocation for the National Institute of Immunology has been kept at Rs.14.00 crores for the year 2000-2001 as
 against Rs.13.00 crores as was in B.E. and R.E. for the  1999-2000.  The Committee wanted to know whether the increase
 of Rs.1 crore would be sufficient to carry on the initiatives the Department  propose to take up during the year under
 review.  In response the Department has  informed that the allocation for the Institute has been increased by Rs. 1 crore,
 which is essential to augment the infrastructure of P-3 laboratory which is  to handle infectious materials as well as
 pathogenic microbes and would be sufficient to augment P-3 laboratory facilities.
33.In reply to a question as to how many of the technologies related to diagnosis of AIDS virus, anti leprosy vaccine etc.
 which were under trial, have yielded desired results and have been transferred to industry for pilot level production, the
 Committee was informed that three diagnostic technologies developed under DBT supported programme on HIV/AIDS
 have been transferred to three industries for further refinement/pilot level production.  The technology of anti-leprosy
 vaccine has been transferred to M/s Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd. after obtaining regulatory clearances.  The anti-leprosy
 vaccine as immunomodulator is being marketed by this concern as Leprovac.  The contraceptive candidate vaccine,  Beta

 formulation so as to obtain predictable and sustainable immune responses in vaccinated women.  The improvement of the

34.The Committee is satisfied with the work being done by the National institute of Immunology.  However it observes that
 there are  certain unexplored areas in the field of  Immunodiagnostics and other diseases, where the institute can focus its
 research activities.  The Committee has been made to understand that 80% of all the R&D and scientific research is

 additional support to Research activities.
NATIONAL BRAIN RESEARCH CENTRE (NBRC)
35.A budgetary allocation of Rs.5.00 crores has been sought for NBRC.  Asked about the priorities which have necessitated
 the enhanced allocation, the Committee has been  informed that the basic theme of the Centre is to understand brain, to
 protect brain and to create  brain.  During the financial year 1999-2000 various activities in generation of manpower were
 initiated under Medical Biotechnology.  The Department proposes to undertake research  in the identified priority areas
 during the financial year 2000-2001.  This would be on computational neurosciences, developmental neurosciences, and
 cognitive neurosciences.  The centre has currently initiated research work at the ICGEB campus.  The NRBC would utilise
 some of the unfinished building structures after appropriate re-modelling at IVCOL site.  At the same time hitech
 laboratories are also proposed to be constructed at Manesar, Gurgaon.
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR PLANT GENOME RESEARCH (NCPGR)
36.The Committee was informed that NCPGR, an autonomous research institution is presently carrying out its research
 activities from the  Centre of Plant Molecular Biology of Jawaharlal Nehru University.  The Centre has initiated the work
 for analysing chickpea genome, identifying genes, develop suitable regeneration protocols for improving the nutritional
 quality and resistance against various diseases and a biotic stresses.  More than 100 ESTs have been sequenced from
 chickpea.  
37.The Committee is of the view that Agriculture is not really sustainable anywhere on account of loss of top soil and
 excessive use of pesticides and fertilizers besides growth of population at a rapid pace.  Hence the need for higher
 productivity and for nutritious food. The object can be achieved by changing the plant characteristics by genetic
 modification.  The Committee impresses upon the Department to work with full vigour in this area and efforts should be
 made to cover  value based crops under its ambit which may solve the problem of under nourishment  at the glassroot levels
 of the society.
38.After making a detailed scrutiny of the Demands for Grants of the Department of Biotechnology and assessing the
 progress of various important programmes and projects administered by it, the Committee recommends that the Demands
 for Grants of Rs.136.08 crores as sought by the Department of Biotechnology for the current financial year, under Demand
 No.75 may be approved.
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS AT GLANCE
 
1.   The Committee observes that the demand for biotech products has been steadily increasing and counting with country’s
 tremendous potential of biodiversity, scientific and technical manpower and existing infrastructure it is likely to become an
 important global player in biotechnology in the next 10 years or so.  Keeping the mandate of the Department in view the
 Committee feels that sufficient funds need to be provided to the Department so that it can carry out its  mission effectively.
(Para 7)
2.   The Committee feels that with the rising  costs of chemical fertilisers and the accompanying  risks of degradation of soil
 fertility because of increasing resource of these fertilisers, the role of biofertilisers and biopesticides is becoming
 significant.  The Committee recommends that the Department should encourage  the use of biofertilisers and biopesticides
 by educating the farmers though Print & Electronic media and field demonstrations, so as to achieve higher consumption
 levels of the bioproducts and with a view to increase their yields.
(Para 11) 
3.   The Committee feels that with a view to replenish  the depleting forest cover and improve the environment  the role of
 tissue culture technique  has assumpted importance.  The committee observes that the techniques if proved successful in
 case of ongoing projects, may be replicated in  case of value based forest trees, horticultural crops and plantation crops.
(Para 14)

R E P O R T
           
      Information Technology (IT) has tremendous potential to become an engine of growth and productivity improvement for
 all sectors of the economy and for the country.  With the continued thrust on liberalization, in order to make IT products
 cost effective and  price competitive, the  use and penetration of computers in the society is fast expanding with special
 emphasis on multi-lingual technologies.
2.   Ministry of Information Technology was set up on 15 th October, 1999 to be the nodal institutional mechanism for
 facilitating all the initiative in the Central Government, the State Government, Academia, the Indian private sector and
 successful Indian IT professionals abroad.  With a view to accelerate the Internet revolution in India, emphasizing the
 creation of useful contents in Indian languages, IT-enabled services, IT education, electronics and computer hardware
 manufacturing and exports, silicon facility, e-Commerce and Internet based enterprises, the Ministry has been entrusted the
 task of implementation of a comprehensive action plan to make India an IT Superpower in the early part of the next century
 and achieve a target of $ 50 billion in software exports by 2008.
      The Ministry has been entrusted with the following responsibilities:-
(i)            Policy matters relating to IT;
(ii)        Promotion of knowledge based enterprises, Internet, e-commerce, IT education and IT based education;
(iii)            Development of Electronics;
(iv)            Development of Microelectronics and Silicon facility;
(v)            Promotion of Information Technology and Standardization;
(vi)            National Informatics Centre (NIC); and
(vii)            Electronics and Computer Software Export Promotion Council (ESC)
In order to make India an IT Super Power by the Year 2008, the vision translates into a mission-‘Move works to India’. 
 The Vision objective are:
(i)            Creation of Wealth
(ii)            Employment Generation
(iii)            IT led Economic Growth
The role of the Ministry of IT will be of a
(i)            Pro-active facilitator
(ii)            Pro-active motivator
(iii)            Pro-active promoter
(iv)            Spread of IT to masses speedily and

3.   Investment in knowledge based industries will determine a country’s dominance in the next century.  The software
 industry  has  emerged  as  one of  the fastest  growing  sectors  in  the economy with Cumulative Annual Growth Rate
 (CAGR) exceeding 50% over the last five years and with a likely turnover of US$ 6 billion and exports of US$ 4 billion
 during 1999-2000.  The Government has targeted an export of US$ 50 billion by the year 2008 for the Indian software
 industry.

 crores Non-Plan) for 1999-2000.  The allocation for the year 2000-2001 is thus Rs.197.20 crores more than R.E. of 1999-
2000.

 outlay of Rs.2.25 crores and Rs.10.00 crores has been provided for initiating Information Technology Certification and
 Information Technology Brand Equity Fund (IBEF) respectively.  IBEF is proposed to be set up with the objective to make
 ‘Made in India’ label a symbol of quality, competitive price, reliability and service to the customers.  In addition, a
 provision of Rs.142.17 crores and Rs.2.00 crores has been made for National Informatics Centre (NIC) and Electronics and
 Computer Software Export Promotion Council (ESC) respectively.  These organizations have now been brought under the
 administrative control of the Ministry since October, 1999.

NATIONAL INFORMATICS CENTRE (NIC)
5.   National Informatics Centre (NIC) which was set up in 1977, is a premier S&T organization of the Government of India
 in the field of Informatics Services and Information Technology (IT) applications in India. NIC was a constituent unit under
 the erstwhile Department of Electronics and then brought under the Planning Commission in 1988. It is now a part of the
 Ministry of Information Technology.  Its main objective is to provide computer support to Central Government
 Departments, State Government Departments, District Administration and new districts being created by the State
 Governments.  NIC has set up a satellite based computer communication network for providing E-mail, INTERNET, File
 Transfer access to  National & International databases etc.  NIC has set up a Local Area Networks(LAN) in Central
 Government Departments and State Government Secretariats.  NIC has been training the Government employees on a
 regular basis to enable them to use MIS databases.  Training is provided upto district level.  It is the only Government
 Organization in India, at present, offering network services over C-band and Ku-band VSATs, Wireless Metropolitan Area
 Networks and Local Area Networks (LANs) with NICNET gateway for Internet resources, so as to promote  social,
 economic, scientific and technological activities, and also for “macro-economic adjustment programme” of the
 Government.
5.1Since its inception, NIC has been propagating “IT-led Development” facilitating rapid economic growth and social
 transformation in India, by setting up a countrywide satellite based VSAT network (NICNET), first of its kind among the
 developing countries, linking about 540 District Administrations, 25 State Secretariats, and 7 NCT/UT Administrations. 
 NICNET links extend to Andaman Islands, Lakshadweep & Minicoy Island , Ladhakh Region, Indian High  Commission
 (Mauritius), and B.P. Koirala Institute of Medical Sciences in Kathmandu (Nepal).  NIC provides the state-of-the-art IT
 solutions to information management, information dissemination, and decision support requirements of the Central as well

5.3In some of the offices there is a large accumulation of hardware such as computer terminals, keyboards and related
 material such as transformers etc. which contained software, which is not in use now because of the upgradation of
 technology.  This material is now lying as junk for so many years with no action for its removal in sight.   Unless urgent
 steps are taken for the disposal of the hardware, which appears to have been rendered obsolete, it may pose an
 environmental hazard, more so because of the rapid advances being made in this field.  When asked about removal of this
 material lying in the Government offices, the Committee was informed that the NIC has set up a Obsolete Declaration
 Committee to identify obsolete equipments and outdated software and recommend their disposal.  It has also set up an
 Auction Committee to expedite the auction of the items recommended as obsolete by the Obsolete Declaration Committee.
5.4The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that the provision of Rs.142.17 crores for the NIC for the year 2000-01 is
 sought to be utilized mainly towards its on-going activities.  If it be so, the Committee fails to understand as to how NIC
 will catch up with rapid advances being made in this field as a result of technical innovations.  The Committee therefore
 observes that the Ministry should review its priorities and, if necessary, come out with additional financial projections at
 R.E. stage.  The Committee feels that financial constraints should not be allowed to stay in the way of IT culture being
 spread in the country or in the matter of gaining supremacy in the field.
5.5       The attention of the Secretary, Ministry of Information Technology was drawn to the following recommendation of
 the Committee contained in its Sixty-seventh Report:
“The Committee finds that the Planning Commission has sanctioned a budget support of Rs.300 crores for Information

 of the Ministry/Department of Government of India.  The Department is working on so many programmes/projects
 concerning Information Technology such as ERNET, NII, TDIL, Electronic Commerce, Electronic Governance, Venture
 Capital for Software etc. and the Planning Commission have not allocated sufficient funds for the said
 programmes/projects.  As DOE is responsible for promotion of Information Technology in the country, the Committee is
 strongly of the view that the amount of Rs.300 crores provided by the Planning Commission to be spent during the Ninth
 Plan may be allocated under the administrative control of Department of Electronics and the Department may be designated
 as a nodal agency in the field of Information Technology.”
In the Action Taken Report, the Ministry has informed as follows:
      “…… the matter was taken up with the Planning Commission in June’99 to allocate funds for IT in the IX Plan under the
 administrative control of the Department of Electronics.  The Planning Commission has constituted a group to work out
 modalities to be adopted for allocation of funds under the new Plan Scheme for development of IT.  Ministry of Information
 Technology has since been set up to addresses all policy matters and promotion of IT in the country.  In view of this
 development, Planning Commission has been approached again to place funds under the Ministry of Information
 Technology”.

 Commission has been approached again to place funds under the Ministry of IT.

6.   The Technology Development Council (TDC) programme  seeks to support the new initiatives responding to changing
 developmental needs of the electronics sector keeping in line with the liberalized industry policy framework.  The
 programme aims to promote and support research, design, development and engineering in the areas of computer and
 computer communications, control and instrumentation, consumer electronics telecommunications and broadcasting.
6.1When asked about the disproportionate variations in respect of TDC programme, the committee was informed that the
 original provision during 1999-2000 for TDC programme was Rs.8.00 crores (6.80 crores as grants-in-aid and Rs.1.20
 crores as loan), which was reduced to Rs.4.00 crores in R.E. (Rs.3.30 crores as grants-in-aid and Rs.0.70 crores as loan). 
 The reduction in provision has been in view of new project proposals from some of the implementing organisations having
 not materialized and delay in release of funds from some of the ongoing projects owing to funds already available with
 some of the institutes against the earlier releases.  The provision for 2000-01 has been proposed at Rs.5.00 crores (Rs.3.00
 crores as grants-in-aid and Rs.2.00 crores as loan)  which would be utilized mainly towards the ongoing projects and  new
 projects.
 
6.2The Committee observes that it is necessary to ensure perfect co-ordination among the    project implementing agencies 
 supported under TDC programme.  This could be reflected only when allocation made during the period under review is
 utilized fully.
INDUSTRIAL ELECTRONIC PROMOTION PROGRAMME
7.   The Industrial Electronics Promotion Programme (IEPP) aims at development and application of Electronics &
 Information Technology based products and systems to improve productivity, quality and safety in the industrial sector. 
 Under the programme, generic technologies applicable to all industry in general as well as industry specific technologies for
 example meant for paper, textile and steel industries are developed and implemented.  System engineering projects are also
 taken up to enhance productivity, conserve energy and improve quality.
7.1The Committee was informed that the allocation for IEPP was reduced from Rs.3 crores in B.E. of 1999-2000 to Rs.2
 crores in R.E. of that year due to some of the new projects having  not materialised   for want of some clarifications.  The
 Committee was apprised that the B.E. for 2000-2001 has again been increased to Rs.3 crores as seven ongoing projects
 would be completed in the current year and six other projects would be nearing completion by 2000-2001.   New project
 initiatives have been taken in the area of Coal Mining and Food Industry.
7.2The Committee was also informed that with emphasis on Information Technology implementation, IEPP programme

8.   Information Infrastructure is vital for the country and has a tremendous potential for bringing rapid transformation in our

 enhancing overall efficiency in work, reduce delays in decision making, promote optimal utilization of manpower resources
 by improving access to information and Information Technology tools and  demonstrate the concept in action to other
 users.  Some of the sectors proposed to be covered under the programme include, literacy, education and life-long learning
 leading to increase in employment opportunities, better health care, environment friendliness, opportunities for rural
 populace to acquire new skills etc.  A number of initiatives have also been taken in the area of multi-media promotion,
 electronic governance and ATM test bed.
8.1The allocation for NII during 2000-2001 has been kept at Rs.11.00 crores as against Rs.10.00 crores in B.E. and Rs.6.00
 crores in the R.E. of the year 1999-2000.  The Committee was informed that the enhanced allocation for the NII programme
 during 2000-2001 is because of the requirement of the network security and also towards new test-beds/applications
 projects and promotional measures  towards e-commerce implementation, online learning amongst others.  Three new 
 projects are also in progress for development of e-commerce technology, tourism information system and creation of
 information infrastructure for Sikkim Government.  Certain new projects in the field of telephony overy internet, networks
 security, e-commerce applications and web enabled database management are being initiated. 
8.2The Committee notes that an allocation of Rs.10 crores was made for NII at B. E. stage of the year 1999-2000 which was
 reduced to Rs.6 crores at the R.E. of that year and it has again been increased to Rs.11 crores in 2000-01.  In view of  the
 variations in the allocation, it appears that either the Ministry is not following realistic approach towards the programme or
 there has been   utilization of funds due to  other reasons.  The Committee therefore reiterates its earlier observation made in
 its 67
th Report and would like to emphasize that having once drawn up the programmes, the Ministry should aim at full
 utilization of the budgetary provisions.    
8.3  The Committee observes that logging into the Internet in Delhi through telephone numbers announced by NIC and in
 the North-eastern region is next to impossible in view of poor telecom infrastructure.  A decision was taken by VSNL to set

 about the project and there appears no physical progress.  The Committee therefore recommends that the International
 gateway should be commissioned within a definite time frame.   Efforts should also be made to improve accessibility to the
 internet through telephone network as an individual subscriber may not have the advantage of LAN.

th Report of the Committee that Disinvestment

SOCIETY FOR APPLIED MICROWAVE ELECTRONICS ENGINEERING AND RESEARCH (SAMEER)
10.SAMEER , with three Centres at Mumbai, Chennai and Calcutta, is engaged in focused R&D in specific areas of
 microwave engineering, millimeter waves  and applied electromagnetics.  It also undertakes development of components
 subsystem/system and integrated large systems for meeting specific requirements in Defence, Space and Meteorology. It
 has been working in the thrust areas such as, microwave and RF applications in industry, instrumentation and health, linear
 accelerator technology, millimeter wave and integrated opto-electronics technologies, electromagnetic compatibility
 meteorology, antennas, thermal and industrial design of electronic products, etc.  At SAMEER the activities are prioritized
 towards resource generation and special attention to the core R&D areas.  So, SAMEER has maintained its lead in the area
 of EMI/EMC and RF/Microwave technology.  SAMEER has also got a contract for consultancy and electromagnetic
 ambient survey at Jordan. 
10.1The allocation for SAMEER during the year 2000-01 has been kept at Rs.8 crores as compared to B.E. as well as R.E.

SOFTWARE/HARDWARE EXPORT PROMOTION
11.The programme aims at the creation of basic facilities for development and export of software to data links and promote
 integrated development of software/hardware in the country for domestic as well as export market.  Computer software
 remains a thrust area and the fastest growing sector both in export and domestic sector.  Software Export has risen to
 Rs.17,000 crores during 1999-2000 from Rs.10,940 crores during 1998-99, registering a growth rate of over 55%. Domestic
 Software industry is likely to go up to Rs.7,300 crores during 1999-2000 from Rs.4,900 crores  during  1998-99.  The 
 schemes  broadly  covered by  the  programme are : -  a)  Software Infrastructure (STPs); b) Quality Assurance,
 Certification and Information Security Management; c) Development support for software (R&D); and Export Promotion
 Campaigns and Markets Intelligence studies.
11.1Asked about the reasons for enhanced allocation for the said programme during the year 2000-01, the Committee has
 been informed that the increase in allocation for Software/Hardware Export Promotion (SEPP) from Rs.5.0 crores in B.E.
 and R.E. of 1999-2000 to Rs.7.0 crores in B.E. of 2000-01 is due to expansion of Software Technology Parks of India
 (STPI) infrastructure and setting up of some of the new Software Technology Parks  (STPs) as well as towards launching of
 some new projects.
11.2The Committee has been given to understand that very low investment is coming forward in Hardware industry and
 foreign investment is going to Taiwan, China, Brazil, Malaysia, etc.  The Committee notes that during the year 1999-2000,
 computer software industry has witnessed a growth of 53% whereas it is abysmally low at 10% in hardware industry. 
 While software industry is doing well in the country, there is need to focus attention at hardware production and analyse the
 reasons that tend to block its growth and take remedial steps.  The Committee observes that hardware sector is showing
 reverse trends and as such has made little progress.  The Committee, therefore recommends, the Ministry should endeavour
 to bridge the gap between two sectors by chalking out concrete plans for speedy promotion and development of hardware
 export in the country.
SPECIAL MANPOWER DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME FOR SOFTWARE EXPORT
12.The programme has been launched by the Ministry with the objective to create and strengthen specialized manpower
 required to support growing software export industry and to achieve targeted export.  Under the programme, expansion
 activities of the Bangalore Unit of the National Centre for Software Technology (NCST) have been undertaken to
 strengthen R&D and higher end software education and training.  Other project included in the programme is expansion of
 NCST activities in Navi Mumbai to promote research and development and Advanced Software Education.  This center
 would specialize in the area of Network and Internet Technology, Visual and Artificial Computing.  An advanced one year
 programme in Software Technology has already been initiated.  The budget allocation for the programme during the year
 2000-2001 has been kept at Rs.6.50 crores. 
12.1The future plan under the programme includes, completion of second phase of construction activity for expansion
 project of NCST, Bangalore and first phase of main building for Navi Mumbai.  R&D activity in the identified areas of
 excellence in both centers is also proposed to be initiated.  New programmes relating to ‘Enterprenuers Development Centre
 of IT-Enabled Services’, support to finishing schools, specialized training in Web Designing Software Tools etc. would be
 initiated.
12.2The Committee notes the position with satisfaction.  However, it feels that there is still a scope for publicity for different
 projects under the programme so to educate maximum number of people.  This would help the programme to achieve
 desired results.

 working models were displayed on the “Swarn Jayanti Express” run by the Indian Railways to display the achievements of

EDUCATION AND RESEARCH NETWORK (ERNET)
14.The ERNET Project was initiated in 1986 to strengthen national capabilities in the area of a computer networking and
 data communication, to make it competitive by world standards and to carry the benefits to nationwide academic and
 research community, industry and variety of users.  Today ERNET has about 750 institutions connected to its network.  In
 order to facilitate network access to its users, ERNET Points of Presence (PoPs) are being established in all major cities in
 the country.  Considering the special communication requirement for student community in North East  region of  the
 country, ERNET has taken a special  initiative and established a dedicated satellite Network in the region.  With this,
 isolated Universities and Colleges in this region would be able to reap benefits of Internet revolution round the globe.
14.1     Asked about the constant reduction in the allocation for the programme, the Committee was informed that the
 reduction in financial allocation for Education and Research Network (ERNET) India in R.E. for 1999-2000 to Rs.16.00
 crores from Rs.25.00 crores in B.E. for that year is due to delay in getting 8.2 M bp backbone lines with state-of-art network
 equipment from Department of Telecom.  The outlay from Ministry of Information Technology for ERNET India was
 recommended by Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) at Rs.60.00 crores, based on which the draft CCEA note was
 prepared and circulated to concerned Ministries.  Ministry of  Finance however, desired that the outlay from Government of
 India need to be further reviewed and suitably reduced.  Hence, the revised CCEA through Ministry of Finance.  Against the
 proposed Government support of Rs.19.85 crores, the amounts already been released to  the Society during 1997-98
 (Rs.5.30 crores) and 1998-99 (Rs.14.55 crores) and the likely releases to be made during 1999-2000 were Rs.16.00 crores
 as per R.E.  Thus, the remaining balance to be paid to ERNET India during 2000-2001 and 2001-02 works out to Rs.19.15
 crores only, against which the allocation made in Demands for Grants for MIT for 2000-01 is Rs.15.00 crores and the
 balance of Rs.4.01 crores will be made in 2001-02.
14.2 The Committee feels that initiation of ERNET project is a praiseworthy step as this would facilitate commercial
 exploitation of the technologies by the industries and other users.

15.The Ministry of Information Technology has initiated an Employment Generation Training Scheme for unemployed
 educated youth belonging to SCs, STs, Backward Regions and the North Eastern region including Sikkim.  The objective of
 the Scheme is to generate employment opportunities for the educated unemployed youth by harnessing the potential of
 Electronics and Information Technology.  Under the Scheme, free courses are offered to SC, ST and OBC candidates.
15.1The Committee was informed that the Ministry has identified certain computer hardware and software training courses
 as well as Electronics related repair and maintenance courses for the educated unemployed youths under its Employment
 Generation Training Scheme.  The Committee notes that various institutions in the north-eastern sectors and rural areas
 have been funded under this scheme where IT training is being imparted in the regular batches and the performance is
 satisfactory.
15.2 During 2000-01, the Ministry plans to constitute a task force on distance education at the national level so that IT
 education and IT Enabled education can reach the masses across the country and it provides an opportunity for the
 backward areas in the field of human resource development.
15.3 The Committee finds that the B.E. for the 2000-01 has been reduced to Rs.1 crore as compared to B.E. and R.E. of Rs.4
 crores for 1999-2000. The Committee was informed that reduction in the B.E. of 2000-2001 is due to the reason that the 
 provision  for North-East Projects both on-going/new has been made separately at  Rs.36.52 crores  under the head
 “provision for projects/schemes for the benefit of North-Eastern Region and Sikkim”.

ELECTRONIC GOVERNANCE
16.Electronic Governance Programme started early 1999 by the Ministry with the objective to i) accelerate the usage of
 Electronic Governance in all spheres of Governance thus facilitating public access to Government services with quicker
 responses through single window anywhere anytime approach; ii) examine practical implications of IT related issues in the
 Government thereby improving services to the citizens; iii) identify appropriate hardware platforms and software
 application packages for cost effective delivery   of public through internet; and v) preparation of guidelines on
 standardisation of databases, hardware software etc.  The programme has been included in the annual plan of 1999-2000 of
 the Ministry.  A few pilot projects of E-Governance viz. Citizen-IT Interface, EG model for Indian Universities, IT station
 in states/Departments have been evolved and are progressing further.
16.1 The Committee notes the position with satisfaction.  However, it observes that even though a beginning has been made
 to provide various kinds of services through computers and other sources of IT, it is equally necessary to review at regular
 intervals the quality as well as utility of the softwares to ensure that they are meeting the requirement of the people and
 effect improvements wherever necessary.
17. After considering the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Information Technology and assessing the progress of
 various important programmes and projects administered by it, the Committee recommends that the Demands for Grants of
 Rs.392.20 crores, as sought by the Ministry of Information Technology, for the year 2000-01 under Demand No.56, may be
 approved.

 culture being spread in the country or in the matter of gaining supremacy in the field.

 Commission and appearing the Committee on its part, the Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation (67 th Report)
 that the amount of Rs.300 crores has been sanctioned by the Planning Commission for IT to be spent during the Ninth Five
 Year (1997-2002) period.  The allocation has not been earmarked against any of the Ministry/Department of Government of

 Department of Electronics and the Department may be designated as a  nodal agency in the field of Information
 Technology.

R E P O R T
      The Department of Ocean Development was created in July, 1981 within the Cabinet Secretariat directly under the
 charge of the Prime Minister. In March, 1982 it became a separate Department and has since been functioning as a nodal
 Department for organising, coordinating and promoting ocean development activities in the country, in line with the Ocean
 Policy Statement of 1982. The programmes pursued by the Department over the years have also kept pace with
 developments World over and addressed National needs and issues.
      The programmes of the Department are directed towards:
(i)         Technology Development Programmes for future applications with strategic, industrial and economic
 significance.
(ii)        Societal Programmes with direct/indirect benefit for the community by technology applications and pilot
 project demonstration with the participation of the community for their socio-economic prosperity, and for
 coastal area development.
(iii)       Marine Resources Programmes for exploration of marine living and non-living resources, techno-economic
 studies to evolve strategies for sustainable exploration and utilisation, and resource enhancement.
(iv)       Multi-institutional and multi-disciplinary Polar Science Programmes and Antarctic Expeditions with
 scientific and geo-political significance.
(v)        Capacity Building Programme towards self-reliance through basic scientific research in ocean sector, human
 resource development and establishing Centres of Excellence in academic institutions.
(vi)
              Creation of public awareness on the potential and uses of ocean.

 crores for the other Plan schemes.

15.The Secretary informed the Committee that the 19
th Indian Scientific expedition to Antarctica was launched from Cape
 Town, South Africa, on 9 th December 1999, keeping in view the likely scientific and economic benefits and future
 international cooperation in the field of polar science between India and other countries. The 19 th Expedition to Antarctica
 consisted of a 47 member team including 30 scientists and 17 logistic personnel, under the leadership of Mr. Arun
 Chaturvedi a scientist of Geological Survey of India, including a two member lady team – one medical Doctor from India
 and a Geologist from Peru.  This included a contingent of 25 members who would winter-over in Antarctica for 16 months

16.In addition to the ongoing programmes several new experiments have been initiated during the course of this expedition,
 which includes:
(i)                 Study of earth-air current systems to give an insight to the deep space processes.
(ii)        Experiments on crack propagation of the ice-shelf in order to understand the dynamics and processes of
 Iceberg generation.
(iii)       Installation of a number of automatic weather stations to measure energy balance and albedo factors of the
 ice, as a part of global change studies.
(iv)       Reconstruction of the past climatic and vegetative history through the study of organo-debris present in the
 fresh water lake sediments of Antarctica.
(v)        Establishment of an environment monitoring laboratory for the first time at Maitri in order to carry out an

18.1  The Committee recommends that  the National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research(NCAOR) Goa, should be

DELINEATION OF OUTER LIMITS OF CONTINENTAL SHELF
61.Traditionally the Coastal States had been claiming few nautical miles into the sea.  In accordance with the UN Convention on
 Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), now the States can establish 12 nautical miles of territorial sea and 200 nautical miles of Exclusive
 Economic Zone (EEZ) from baselines and there are no major technical difficulties in establishing the limits.  The States are also
 entitled for the
rights over the continental shelf, slope and rise extending beyond the EEZ.  The continental shelf comprises the seabed and
 subsoil of the submarine areas that extend beyond the territorial sea throughout the natural prolongation of the land territory. 
 The continental shelf is rich in non-living resources and the minerals, including hydrocarbon resources.
62.The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea stipulates that where the coastal state intends to establish the outer limits of the
 continental shelf beyond 200 nautical miles, it shall submit particulars of such limits to the Commission on the Limits of
 Continental Shelf (CLCS), along with the supporting scientific and technical data as soon as possible, but in any case within 10
 years of entry into force of the Convention for that State.  The Convention came into force on 16.11.1994 and India ratified the
 same in June 1995.  India thus must submit all the necessary data to the CLCS by June 2005.  If delineation is done properly
 India would be in a position to claim more than 1 million sq.km beyond the EEZ.  India is represented as an elected member on
 the Commission on the Limits of Continental Shelf (CLCS).
63.The Committee observes that with the ratification of the UN Convention on Law of the Sea, a new international order has
 been established for the oceans and  India being represented in almost all the important bodies on oceans will stand to benefit
 enormously by provisions of the convention, only if we can build an integrated approach for scientific planning, formulation,
 implementation and overall management of the programmes with a comprehensive organisational and institutional back up.

 seas. The technology should  be handed over  to the State Governments for continuous operation and maintenance.
(Para 53)
13.       The Committee  shares the perception that the genetic and biotic equilibrium should be maintained in the Indian
 environment.  However, it  is of the view that the Department should carry out further research on formulation of
 appropriate feeds for maximum growth of lobsters and also develop the  larval rearing technology in Indian spiny lobster. At
 the same time the Department should also implement  projects on development of technology for sustainable shrimp
 farming, lobster and seaweed culture and polyculture of marine organisms at ANCOST.
(Para 60)
14.       The Committee observes that with the ratification of the UN Convention on Law of the Sea, a new international order
 has been established for the oceans and  India being represented in almost all the important bodies on oceans will stand to
 benefit enormously by provisions of the convention, only if we can build an integrated approach for scientific planning,
 formulation, implementation and overall management of the programmes with a comprehensive organisational and
 institutional back up.

R E P O R T
 
 
The Indian Space Programme, since its inception in the early sixties, is geared to achieve the goal of self-reliant use
 of Space Technology to ensure rapid progress in diversified fields of the country including social, economic, cultural and
 scientific for finding solutions to the problems of man and society. Even as India entered the new millennium, the space
 programme in the country has matured to a status where space has become an important element of the national
 infrastructure, especially in the areas of communication, broadcasting, meteorology, disaster management and resources
 monitoring. India is recognized the world over for its unique application driven space programme. Further, industry
 participation in the space programme  has been expanding, bringing economic benefits. The plan to further enhance and
 improve the space services by launching follow-on satellites in the INSAT and IRS series in coming years and to enhance
 the launch capability to place INSAT class of satellites in orbit through GSLV, the Indian Space Programme is well poised
 to play a stronger role in the country's march towards progress in the new millennium.
2.     Whereas the efforts of the Indian Space Programme in the early sixties were confined to getting familiar with space
 technologies and developing technical and organisational infrastructure in order to develop satellite launch vehicles, during
 the eighties, the space programme moved closer to realising the goal of self-reliant use of space technology for national
 development. The country entered the nineties with the launch of more ASLVs and PSLVs. With the launch of IRS-IB and
 INSAT 2A and 2B, the Indian Space Programme becomes fully operational through its own communication and remote
 sensing satellites. The Indian Space Programme is broad-based and it has an impressive array of achievements in putting to
 use space technology for vital applications - for telecommunications, TV broadcasting, weather watching, forecasting
 agricultural crop and forests wealth assessment, water resources management, flood mapping, drought forecasting,
 identification of marine resources, protection of the environment and rural literacy campaign etc.
3.     Self-reliance in space technology has been an important target of the programme from the very beginning.  Long-range
 plans have been drawn up, from the very beginning, for each decade, to steer the programme effectively, ensuring
 appropriate linkages among the application needs, satellite missions, launch vehicle capabilities and technology
 development. Over the last three-and-half decades, significant achievements have been made in country in the area of space
 technology (i) for building world-class satellites for communications and remote sensing, (ii) for launching the remote
 sensing satellites from India with our own launch vehicle and (iii) in reaching  the benefits of space technology to improve
 the quality of life at the grass root level, thus contributing to several areas of national development.  Necessary
 organizational and institutional mechanisms with users, industries and academia have also been established. In tune with the
 goal of self-reliant use of space technology for national development, the thrust areas of the Indian Space Programme are:-
(a)    Satellite-based communication for various applications;
(b)    Satellite-based resources survey and management and environmental monitoring;
(c)    Meteorological applications; and
(d)   Development and operationalisation of indigenous satellites and launch vehicles for
         providing these space services.

4.     The Department of Space, which was set up in 1972 to promote unified development and application of Space Science
 Technology for identified national objectives, is entrusted with the task of implementing the policies framed by the Space
 Commission.   The policies are carried out through the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the three Grant-in-
aid institutions viz., the National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA), the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) and the
 National Mesosphere-Stratosphere-Troposphere Radar facility (NMRF).
5.     Today, the space  sector world over, is poised for a transformation towards a matured, scientific and industrial sector,
 with multiple players and changing roles. Besides, it needs to adapt itself to the implications of a market driven economy
 and the formidable challenges arising out of increased societal needs, technological limitations, resource constraints and
 geo-political scenarios.   In India, while integrating the programmes with the international scenario, the national needs are to
 be addressed; the gains achieved so far have to be consolidated; new and potential areas of space technology utilization are
 to be identified and developed; organisational as well as managerial support have to be ensured to surge forward, harnessing
 national capability and capacity, ensuring synergy amongst the partners as well as space systems.
6.    The Committee observes India is one of the six countries with homemade satellites in orbit. Despite being a new entrant
 to the competitive global space club, which hitherto was an exclusive preserve of a handful of countries, India's overall
 track record both in the field of rocketry and satellites has been impressive. This, of course, does not overlook the fact that it
 had its share of failures too, which needless to say can be expected in any hi-tech project. To cite a few, one can recall the
 failure of the ASLV and of the PSLV.   But these failed missions only proved to be another step on the ladder to success.
 The subsequent flights were a resounding success. This endorsed India's claim to be growing space power. The Committee,
 however, would like the Department to keep the analysis of each failed mission in view so that corrective measures can be
 taken while executing future programmes.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
7.     The Committee was informed that the total expenditure on Space research till the end of Eight Plan Period i.e. from the
 inception in 1962-63 to 1996-97 was Rs.7431.67 crores. During the Eight Plan Period most of the programmatic targets and
 missions have been achieved and the total expenditure incurred on these programmes was Rs.3928.53 crores (Plan
 Rs.3155.74 crores and non-plan Rs.772.79 crores).
8.     It has been stated that the Department of Space had asked for an allocation of Rs.11,000 crores for the Ninth Plan
 period to meet the programmatic requirements of the Department, but the allocation was restricted to Rs.6511.72 crores for
 the entire plan period from 1997 to 2002. This is however subject to review on annual basis by the Planning Commission. In
 the first three years of the 9
th plan, the Department has expended Rs.4,164 crores which is 54% of the total plan outlay.
9.     Analysing the performance of the Department on the basis of the information made available, the Committee found that
 during 1997-98, the Department had utilised the funds to the extent of 99.13 percent. In 1998-99, the fund utilization level
 was about 99.9 per cent. The provisional expenditure for 1999-2000 indicates utilization of funds by the Department. The
 Committee notes with satisfaction that the Department has made optimum utilization of the funds allocated to it during
 1997-98, 1998-99 and 1999-2000.
10.    The programme directions and proposals for Ninth Plan (1997-2002) have been formulated after extensive interactions
 and consultations with user Ministries. The guidelines provided by the Space Commission have been adopted in the process
 of formulation. The Committee was informed that consistent with the programme directions and targets envisaged for the
 Ninth Plan period, the specific activities/projects to be undertaken during the year 2000-2001 have been carefully prioritised
 while working out the B.E. for 2000-2001 which are in pursuance of the Zero Base Budgeting Methodology of the
 Department in formulating the process of annual budgets. The financial allocation for 2000-2001 works out to Rs.2019.22
 crores as against Rs.l725.86crores in the R.E. of 1999-2000 and Rs.1755.00 crores in the B.E. of 1999-2000, which is
 higher by Rs.293.36 crores over the revised estimates and Rs.264.22 crores over the B.E. of 1999-2000 (Annexure).
11.    The major landmark achieved by the Department during the year 1999-2000 is the successful launch of the Indian
 Remote Sensing Satellite, IRS-P4 (Oceansat) alongwith two foreign satellites, one belonging to South Korea and other to
 Germany. The successful mission has not only given the ISRO enough confidence to market its launchers abroad but also
 enhanced the space services to the nation in the areas of telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster
 management and resources survey.
11.1  The Committee observes that these achievements are a feather in the cap of the Department as the launch of three
 satellites in a single flight is a technological achievement and it marks India's entry in the commercial launch market.
INDIAN NATIONAL SATELLITE SYSTEM (INSAT)
12.    The Indian National Satellite System, which was established in 1983 with the commissioning of INSAT-IB, is one of
 the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the world today which is entrusted with the task of providing
 services in the areas of telecommunications, television broadcasting, radio networking and meteorology including disaster

 warning.   The Department of Space (DOS) is responsible for establishment and operation of INSAT space segment.
12.1  The INSAT space segment at present comprises of five satellites besides seven transponders leased from a Thailand
 satellite to further augment the INSAT capacity. Among five satellites, three-INSAT-2A, INSAT-2B and INSAT-2C - are
 built indigenously. The other satellites are INSAT-ID procured from the US and INSAT-2DT acquired from ARABSAT
 organization.
12.2  The INSAT system got a substantial boost in 1999-2000 with the launch and operationalisation of INSAT-2E and the
 launch of INSAT-3B, first of five satellite INSAT-3 series. Launch of INSAT-3B is being advanced to precede that of
 INSAT-3A in order to meet the requirement of extended C-Band transponder capacity. During 2000-2001, Department of
 Space aims to complete the work on INSAT-3A and INSAT-3C. The estimated cash flow requirement in 2000-2001 for
 INSAT-3 project is kept at Rs.635.00 cores.
12.3   In response to a query regarding the Satellite Mapping of Border areas, the Committee was informed that functions of
 satellites are limited to providing pictures of local terrain area.
12.4  Asked about the economic benefits that would accrue from INSAT system to the country, the Secretary, DOS, cited the
 example of INSAT-2 satellites where the country has made an investment of Rs. 1,700 crores and from the present level of
 operations of INSAT system country is getting a return of Rs.2,600 crores which is quite an attractive number in terms of
 our country's needs.
SATELLITE NAVIGATION
13.    Satellite navigation equipment has been made mandatory by the International Civil Aviation Organization on all
 civilian aircraft. It is expected to become operational in many advanced countries in the next few years. In India, the Airport
 Authority of India (AAI) is planning to make them adaptable to the Future Air Navigation System through the introduction
 of Indian Wide Area Differential GPS system. In its endeavour to conform to the standards set out by the International Civil
 Aviation Organisation, the AAI is planning to replace the existing navigational aids with satellite navigation equipment by
 the year 2010.
13.1   Department of Space is playing a vital role in establishing the satellite navigation infrastructure in the country. It has
 sent a preliminary project report on satellite based navigation system to the AAI and is working in close coordination with
 the National Steering Committee on Communications, Navigation and Surveillance Air Traffic Management for giving
 shape to the plan of action.
13.2  The Committee feels that in order to fall in line with international standards, the Department should consider
 establishing a satellite based navigation system as that would facilitate modern air navigation system. The Committee is of
 the view that the Airport Authority of India and the Department of Space should work in close coordination to achieve the
 objective.
INDIAN REMOTE SENSING SATELLITE (IRS)
14.    The Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) system, which was commissioned in 1988, constitutes an important element of
 National Resources Management System (NNRMS) providing continuously space based data related to land, water and
 ocean resources as well as atmospheric observations. The IRS system now comprising five satellites IRS-1B, IRC-1C, IRS-
ID, IRS-P3 and IRS-P4 (Oceansat), forms the largest constellation of remote sensing satellites in the world to undertake
 space based remote sensing. The recent launch of IRS-P4 has opened up new vistas for ocean remote sensing, while the
 next in the series IRS-P5 is exclusively devoted to cartographic applications and IRS-P6 targeted for resources survey.
 These are scheduled for launch in the next couple of years. The application of remote sensing data is being extended to
 more areas in agriculture, forestry, surface and ground water harnessing, geology, urban planning, land use and land cover
 mapping and ocean resources survey flood mapping etc.
14.1   The remote sensing applications in the entire country are carried out under the broad umbrella of National Natural
 Resources Management System (NNRMS). As the effective utilization of IRS database on an operational basis is possible
 with the involvement of the states in setting up appropriate mechanism to integrate the database for effective management
 of natural resources in the states, the idea of State Natural Resources Management System (SNRMS) was conceptualized,
 on the pattern of existing NNRMS. The Government of Uttar Pradesh took the pride of being first in establishing SNRMS.
 States like Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Maharashtra are expected to finalise the process of establishing SNRMS in
 their respective states, in the near future.
14.2  While the Committee appreciates the efforts being made by the Department in augmenting its remote sensing
 capability, what is important is not only the effective management and utilization of natural resources but locating more of
 such resources considering that such resources are on the verge of depletion in the times ahead. The Committee  therefore 
 observes  that  the  efforts  should  be  so  oriented  with emphasis  on mapping more of natural resources as also the
 optimum utilization of the resources already tapped.

INTEGRATED MISSION FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (IMSD)
15.    Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development (IMSD) was initiated in 1992 to generate action plan for sustainable
 development of natural resources in rural areas. The mission is an extension of the pilot studies taken up by the Department
 during 1988-90 in predominantly drought prone/desert districts. Under IMSD, local-specific plans for development of land
 and water resources are generated through integrated analysis of thematic maps generated using remote sensing,
 conventional and socio-economic data and also R&D inputs provided by research institutions.   These locale-specific
 developmental/action plans are generated on watershed/blocks basis, thus covering a geographical area of 84 million
 hectares.
15.1   Asked about the implementation of IMSD programme in problem districts of the country, the Committee was
 informed that the IMSD is extended to 247 areas in 175 districts, out of which 34 districts are covered in full.
15.2  IMSD is mainly carried out in the problem districts of the country and the scope of IMSD is expected to be enlarged in
 a phased manner after detailed review of the progress made so far. Recently, IMSD has been extended to 8 districts of
 Orissa. Plans are also being worked out, in consultation with users to extend IMSD for critical areas (IMSD Phase - III).
 The financial allocation ofRs.1.00 crores in B.E. of 2000-2001 is towards monitoring the implementation of action plans in
 selected watershed and for IMSD Phase - III.
15.3  The Secretary, Department of Space, informed the Committee that the Department was planning to start Development
 Programme under the IMSD scheme in some districts of Jammu & Kashmir.
15.4 The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation (68
th Report) that even though the programme was heading
 towards a right direction, the pace of the programme appeared slow. The Committee feels that the tempo of the programme
 needs to be geared up and it should have time bound targets.
 DISASTER MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
16.    The Disaster Management System (DMS) is visualised to provide the backbone support for management of disasters in
 near-real time and also for disaster zonation studies and effective initiation strategies. Space-based disaster management
 system provides valuable inputs when appropriately integrated with the conventional ground-based systems. In the Ninth
 plan period, the efforts are on to complete a system definition study of the DMS and also conduct pilot experiments for
 establishing a prototype DMS. Plot project on DMS has been initiated in some flood-prone districts of Assam.
16.1   With a view to ensure timely dissemination of weather warnings of impending disaster from approaching cyclones,
 specially designed receivers i.e. Cyclone Warning Dissemination Systems (CWDS) have been installed in the cyclone-
prone coastal areas to disseminate cyclone warning messages directly to the affected areas. . At present 250 CWDS have
 been deployed in various coastal states of India.
16.2  The Secretary, Department of Space, informed the Committee that the Department was reviewing its Disaster
 Management System. In this direction, the Department in cooperation with IMD, was planning to install New Generation
 receiver with Global  Positioning  System  to  track
early movements of cyclones.
16.3  The Secretary, further informed the Committee that after Orissa cyclone, the Department was assisting the relief
 agencies by providing them satellite maps of the area indicating the degree of damage. For flood management the
 Department is embarking on geographical information base. The Department, besides Orissa and Andhra Pradesh, is
 working with the Brahmaputra Flood Control Mission and creating geographical maps in Assam in order to identified flood
 prone areas.
16.4  The Committee is constrained to observe that the perfection in the functioning of the Cyclone Warning Dissemination
 Systems (CWDS) for predicting the contours of the cyclone is yet to be achieved. The country has witnessed the fury of
 weather Gods in the form of cyclones and other weather extremes resulting in tremendous loss of life and property in some
 states. There is thus an imperative need to perfect the system. The projects therefore need to be taken up with sense of
 urgency and, if necessary, in cooperation with other Departments and agencies. The Committee feels that the constraint of
 funds should not be allowed to stand in the totality of these projects.
GEO-SYNCHRONOUS LAUNCH VEHICLE (GSLV) PROJECT
17.   The Geo-Synchronous Launch Vehicle (GSLV) is designed and developed to achieve capability   for     placing    
 INSAT     class     communication     satellites   in   Geo-Synchronous transfer orbit. With the launch of GSLV the country
 is expected to bid in the multibillion  dollar commercial satellite launch market. The GSLV contains three stages - solid
 propellant, liquid propellant and cryogenic engine. The first GSLV flight scheduled for launch from Sriharikota  this year
 would use the Russian-built engine and stages.  The second cryogenic engine has also been developed and was awaiting

 transportation from Russia.
17.1   The sanctioned cost for GSLV project is Rs.1105.30 crores and by the end of 1999-2000 the cumulative expenditure
 of the project was estimated to be Rs.1071.05 crores. Thus, a substantial part of the total project cost has already been
 incurred. However, the GSLV project has successfully completed all the developments and has entered the flight hardware
 realisation phase.
17.2  The Committee notes that operationalisation of GSLV would result in India's future INSAT satellites being launched
 by this vehicle. This is expected to result in substantial savings of foreign exchange and rid the country of its dependence on
 foreign technology. Further the capability to launch the INSAT Class of communication satellites, it should enable the
 country to sell the GSLV to other countries for launching their INSAT-type satellites.
CRYO-UPPER STAGE (CUS) PROJECT
18.   The Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS) Project, approved in 1994, was intended to achieve a stage carrying 12.5 tonnes of
 propellant and produce a thrust of 7.5 tonnes. It is expected that GSLV will put INSAT Class of satellites into geostationary
 transfer orbit. The objective of the CUS Project is to develop and qualify a restartable cryogenic stage for the upper stage of
 GSLV. A cryogenic engine which provides one and half times more specific impulse  than conventional space engines, is
 necessary for launching GSLV. Apart from being far more efficient, and enabling heavier payloads to be injected into
 farther orbits, cryogenic engines are cost effective  and are also environment friendly.
18.1   The Committee was informed mat the allocation for the project during the year 2000-01 has been reduced because
 certain materials required for the cryo stage development to be procured from foreign sources could not be realized because
 the tendering action did not result in acceptable quotations and hence had to be retendered. In view of the above, the cash-
flow requirement for the project for RE 1999-20000 had been reduced.
18.2   The Secretary, DOS, informed the Committee that out of approved project cost of Rs.335.89 crores, during the last six
 years i.e. from 1994 to 2000, Rs.251.65 crores have been spent on the development of the project and the Department is
 expected to achieve the first cryogenic stage by the year 2003.
18.3   The first indigenously fabricated cryogenic engine was put on test on 16 February, 2000 at Mahendragiri. While the
 engine was successfully ignited after meticulous preparation, the test was aborted at 11 seconds due to a leak in hydrogen.
 This is the first of  the series of qualification tests for Cryogenic engine. The recorded results will enable suitable corrective
 action to be identified.
18.4  The Committee observes that there is imperative need for the country to perfect its cryogenic capabilities. Sustained
 effort and perseverance should help in that direction. Added to this the analysis of past experiments would act as a guidance
 to the future.
DIRECT - TO- HOME (DTH) TV MISSION
19.    The basic concept of a Direct-to-Home Television Broadcasting Satellite System is a high power satellite operating in
 the KU-Band for direct broadcasting of TV programmes to homes. Responding to the Indian broadcasting industry's
 demand. Government permitted import of KU-Band equipment in 1996 but banned the import in the subsequent year. Since
 then the mission has not made any remarkable progress. The imperative for such a decision is stated to be the need to have a
 comprehensive broadcasting law on the subject. Further, due to decision of the Government not to fund the programme, its
 success depends on the participation of private investors, but this can be achieved only after the law in this regard has been
 enacted.
19.1   The Committee feels that the Government should clear the fog on the issue as early as possible or else its credibility to
 spread information technology is bound to suffer. DTH is a part of information technology and Government should clear the
 hurdles on the subject keeping the interest of the viewers uppermost while enacting any taw on the subject.

 Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) and Geo- Synchronous Satellite launch Vehicle (GSLV) and would also enable
 launch of advanced launch vehicle to Geo-synchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO) with capability to launch four tones class
 satellite. The purpose of the project is to establish a second launch Pad at Sriharikota. The project was sanctioned in 1997
 with a cost of Rs.289.00 crores. The facilities conferred by the project are launch pad with jet deflector, vehicle assembly
 bay, check-out system, propellent and gas storage and transfer facilities for earth storable etc. The budgetary allocation for
 the project in the year 2000-2001 has been kept at Rs.125.65 crores in comparison to meagre allocation of Rs.23.35 crores
 at RE stage, whereas at BE stage the amount was Rs.83.25 crores.
