            In the meeting held on 9th April, 2001, the Committee considered the draft Action Taken Report and adopted the same.
 
 
 
NEW DELHI                                                                                                                            C. RAMACHANDRAIAH,
April 9, 2001                                                                                                                             Chairman,
                         Committee on Science & Technology,
                  Environment & Forests.          
 R E P O R T
 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Ocean Development on the recommendations
 contained in the Seventy-sixth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology,
 Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2000-2001) of the Department of Ocean Development which was presented to the
 Rajya Sabha on 24th April, 2000.  There are fourteen recommendations contained in the Seventy-sixth Report of the Committee.
 Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on 20th December, 2000.
      On scrutiny of the Action Taken Report as received from the Department of Ocean Development, the Committee has observed that
 the Department of Ocean Development has initiated the action for implementation of all fourteen recommendations contained in the
 Seventy-sixth Report of the Committee.
       The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the
 Department of Ocean Development are given in the succeeding paragraphs: -
Budgetary Allocations for 2000-01
Recommendation 
       The Committee recommends that in order to ensure continuity of the Programmes an additional allocation may be allotted
 to the Department at the time of R.E. stage so that rescheduled programmes can be completed in the current year itself.
(Para  11)
Action Taken by the Department
Noted. The observations are being conveyed to the Ministry of  Finance and Planning Commission.
Comments
The Committee  is constrained to note the lackadaisical attitude of the Department in communicating its recommendation to the
 appropriate quarters.  It was in fact in Department’s own interest to expeditiously follow up the recommendation.  But it appears from
 the communication dated the 20 th December, 2000 of the Department that recommendations were still in the process of being
 communicated when RE stage was over and government was in the process of initiating its thinking process for the next budget.
Polar Sciences – Antarctic Expedition
Recommendation
       The Committee observes that this heralds another scientific feat in the realms of polar science at the end of this millennium
 and demonstrates the capabilities and interest of the country to pursue a well-focused scientific campaign from a pristine
 scientific platform provided by Antarctica.
       The Committee recommends that the National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research (NCAOR) Goa, should be
 designated as the nodal  agency of the Department in planning, coordinating and executing the XX Indian Scientific
 Expedition to Antarctica for continuation  of  the  scientific/research programmes   initiated  during the  XIX expedition.  
 
 
The Committee  hopes that the scientific and logistics co-operation gained with the launching of the XIX Expedition from Cape
 Town would lead to the initiation of state-of-the-art research programmes in Polar Sciences and should be carried forward in
 initiating and executing specific and specialized programmes in the scientific disciplines of Polar Remote Sensing, Southern
 Ocean Oceanography & Paleoclimatology, and Antarctic Global Change.
(Para 18 &18.1)
Action Taken by the Department
The Department is grateful for the kind observations. The NCAOR is the Nodal Agency  for planning, coordinating and executing

file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/85th.html[29-08-2018 16:17:22]
 the XX  Indian Antarctic Expedition.  NCAOR is committed to excellence in the polar Sciences.
Comments
      The Committee notes the reply.
Marine Living Resources
Recommendation
       The Committee observes that under Marine Living Resources programme the department would continue its research
 towards studies to establish techniques for estimation of fish, zooplankton and Deep Scattering Layer (DSL) of the biomass;
 large marine ecosystem studies of the Arabian Sea; assessment of mesopelagic  resources of the high seas and studies on the
 benthic productivity/biodiversity and the fish biodiversity of the continental slope area.
(Para 25)
Action Taken by the Department
      The Department of Ocean Development has formulated Marine Living Resources programme in consultation with Ministry of
 Agriculture and will cover subjects mentioned in the observations of the Committee without duplicating the efforts of other
 Departments like Department of Animal Husbandry and  Dairying or Biotechnology.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Drugs from Sea
Recommendation
      The Committee notes with satisfaction that under the programme the Department has done a commendable work.  The
 Committee trusts that the Department would continue the exploratory work relating to collection, identification and bio-
evaluation of the marine flora and fauna from the Indian coastal waters besides completing regulatory pharmacology and
 toxicology of the anti-diabetic and anti-diarrhoeal drug in the year ahead.  This would go a long way in strengthening  the
 commercialization of Indian drugs and their quality comparable to world standards.  The Department should also strive for
 Patenting of anti-cholesterol molecule and achieve the Patenting of Process for anti-HIV drug by Indian Institute of Chemical
 Technology (IICT), Hyderabad. 
(Para 27)
 
Action Taken  by the Department
The Department of Ocean Development (DOD) is grateful to the Committee for their encouraging comments.  Exploratory work
 relating to collection, identification and bioevaluation of marine flora and fauna from Indian coasts is progressing  with Central Drug
 Research Institute, Lucknow as the nodal institution for the DOD project.
    The regulatory Pharmacology work on the identified Antidiabetic and Antidiarrhoeal preparations are complete.  Both the
 preparations are safe and do not show any undesirable effects on cardiovascular and central nervous system at the effective doses. 
 Three months-repeat dose treatment (toxicity) studies on both the preparations in rat are over.  Drug treatment have been well
 tolerated by animals.  Detailed histopathological examinations of organs and tissues are presently under progress.  The mandatory 3
 months repeat dose study in monkey by oral route on these two preparations will be undertaken when permission from the Committee
 for Prevention of Cruelty to Small and Experimental Animals (CPCSEA) is available.
    On anti-cholesterol molecule, an Indian Patent has already been taken (Patent 1371/Cal/97-A SI. No.181673) by the Principal
 Investigator of Calcutta University.
Comments
      The Committee appreciates the effort being made by the Department in  augmenting its efforts in  collection, identification and
 bioevaluation of marine flora and fauna from Indian coasts towards 
Antidiabetic and Antidiarrhoeal preparations. What is
 important in this process is the Department should concentrate its efforts towards  the transfer of technology for
 commercialization to the pharmaceutical  companies at the earliest. At the same time it should be available to the common
 people at  a  moderate price.  Delay caused in finalisation and marketing of such formulations could render the progress and
 efforts made so for, in fructuous, as private sector is always quick in such matters with a view to earn profits.
Marine Non-Living Resources-Polymetallic Nodule Programme
Recommendation
The Committee recommends that the Department should continue its efforts for development of technology for mining
 development of an integrated mining complex module of 25,000 tonnes/yr. capacity for 6000 m. depth in joint collaborative
 efforts so that the cost of Deep Seabed Mining system is reduced significantly.  The Department should also continue its efforts

file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/85th.html[29-08-2018 16:17:22]
 towards commissioning of the design, development and testing of unmanned submersible capable of working up to 6000 m
 through collaborative programme.
(Para 33)
Action Taken by the Department
      A shallow bed mining system developed jointly by National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai and Institute of
 Konstruction (IKS), University of Siegen, Germany was tested off Tuticorin at 410 mts. The system has further been tested
 for its continuous operation, maneuverability etc at a shallower depth. Design of an integrated mining system for operation at
 6000 mts. is underway under this joint Programme with IKS.
     
      Under the collaborative programme between NIOT and Experimental Design Bureau of Oceanological Engineering (EDBOE),
 Russian Academy of Science, project for the design, development and test of an unmanned submersible for operation up to 6000 mts.
 water depth  at a cost of Rs. 18.20 crore is  proposed.
Comments
      
The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department in developing shallow bed mining system developed jointly by
 National Institute of Ocean Technology, Chennai and Institute of Konstruction (IKS), University of Siegen, Germany but
 efforts must be intensified not only to achieve continuous operation, maneuverability etc at a shallower depth of an integrated
 mining system for operation at 6000 mts. for extraction of Poly-Metallic Nodules at that level but also periodical evaluation
 of the project with regard to its economics in the fast changing world.
Recommendation
      The Committee notes with satisfaction the R&D activities of the Department for optimization of extraction efficiencies of
 metal values (Cu., Ni.,Co,.Mn.) at NML(J), RRL(B) and HZL(U) and hopes that the data generated in the demonstration plant
 and associated R&D work in other laboratories for selective scale up studies would be analysed with an ultimate objective of
 designing a commercial plant.
(Para 33.1)
Action Taken by the Department
      In the development endeavor for the extraction of metals from nodules, R&D work towards optimization of extraction efficiency
 continues at Regional Research Laboratory (RRL), Bhubaneshwar, Hindustan Zinc Ltd, Udaipur and National Metallurgy Laboratory,
 Jamshedpur. A Turnkey contract for the setting up a continuous demonstration plant of 500 kg/day capacity has been awarded and the
 plant is scheduled to be commissioned in May, 2001 at HZL, Udaipur for  validation of the Process Package evolved by  RRL,
 Bhubaneshwar & BARC, Trombay.  The Process Parameters to be generated in the Proposed Pilot Plant would be an input for techno-
economic study.
Comments
      The Committee expresses its satisfaction on the efforts made towards R&D work for optimization of extraction  of  Metals. The
 Department should monitor effectively the progress of proposed plant to be commissioned in May, 2001 at Hindustan Zinc Ltd,
 Udaipur for   validation of the Process Package evolved by  RRL, Bhubaneswar & BARC, Trombay to avoid any cost over-run of the
 project.
Marine Environmental and Coastal Zone, Coastal Ocean Monitoring& Prediction Systems (COMAPS)
Recommendation
The Committee doubts the claim of the department particularly in respect of pollution of sea water at Bombay where one
 sees for about 25 minutes of journey on helicopter the water being totally polluted and recommends that Geographical
 Information System based information  system  for monitoring  pollution  in  the coastal  waters need to be carried  out
 
 
with a concerted effort  and a sense of urgency and the data to draw inference on the levels of pollutants in different parts of
 the coastal ocean should be processed and the knowledge so generated should be disseminated to the State Pollution Control
 Boards whenever the pollution levels reach alarming levels for remedial action.  The State Pollution Control Boards should
 also prepare Action Plan for mitigation of coastal pollution. 
(Para 35)
Action Taken by the Department
      The results obtained from the COMAPS programme in the section 0-25 km of Mumbai indicated that the sea beyond 5 km is clean
 compared to the pollution levels observed near the coast.  The suggestion made by the Committee for developing a GIS based

file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/85th.html[29-08-2018 16:17:22]
 Information System is being followed up and the Information System is under development  through NIO, Goa. 
      Data collected is being disseminated to the State Pollution Control Boards indicating the trend of pollution from year to year, as
 suggested by the Committee. Such efforts will be intensified through the above said GIS based Information System. 
The Ministry of   Environment   and Forests are being apprised of the  need   for State   Pollution Control Boards to prepare Action
 Plans  for  mitigation of coastal pollution.
Comments
      The Committee observes that there is a need for greater co-ordination between the Department of Ocean Development  and 
 respective State Pollution Control Boards for a continued monitoring of marine-pollution levels and the data generated through
 Geographical Information Systems (GIS) must be utilised to the fullest extent to achieve desired results.
Coastal  Research Vessels
Recommendation
      The Committee observes that the cruises involved by Coastal Research Vessel (CRV)  Sagar Purvi & Sagar Paschimi
 should be carried on frequent basis to monitor Pollution and they should be carried out with the participation of the scientists
 of Central Electrochemical Research Institute, Karaikudi and National Institute of Oceanography and other related
 institutions.  The cruises should also observe critically the habitats including flora and fauna specially sea turtles in
 Lakshdweep Islands.
(Para 38)
Action Taken by the Department
      The suggestion made by the Committee to use CRV Sagar Purvi and Sagar Paschimi to monitor the pollution with the
 environmental institutions like NIO, CECRI is  being implemented.  A separate cruise programme for Lakshadweep Islands is also
 planned in the year 2000-01 for monitoring the critical habitats like coral reefs, sea turtles etc. in the Lakshadweep Islands like
 Kadamat.
 
Comments
      The Committee notes the reply and is of the view that the Department  should frequently monitor the Pollution levels and
 should try to cover maximum number of the islands spread over Indian coastline in near future.
Development of GIS System for Critical Habitats
Recommendation
      The Committee recommends that under the programme Integrated Coastal and Marine Area Management (ICMAM), the
 Department should complete development of Environmental Impact Assessment guidelines for  waste  disposal,  marine 
 transportation and tourism  sector.  The  task towards determination of Waste Assimilation Capacity should also be carried
 out through development of Geographical Information System.
(Para 42)
Action Taken by the Department
      Under the project on Development of EIA Guidelines for coastal activities, guidelines for activities like ports and harbours, waste
 disposal and tourism are being taken up.  The guidelines for ports and harbours  have been completed  and at present the guidelines for
 waste disposal  and tourism are being developed.  Further, the results of the   Waste Assimilation Capacity project  indicating  the
 various  quantum of wastes to be  disposed and the likely area of disposal by  Industries and  municipalities  will also be developed
 using GIS.
Comments
      The Committee expresses satisfaction that the guidelines for ports and harbours  have been completed  and  the guidelines for
 waste disposal  and tourism are being developed.  The Committee appreciates the progress made so far and would like the work to be
 completed as expeditiously as possible.
Ocean Observations and Information Service (OOIS)
Recommendation
      While the Committee notes with satisfaction that the programme under the Ocean Observation Information Service have
 been successful, it observes that the indigenisation of Data buoy technology and Operation and maintenance of 12 data buoy
 system by National Data Buoy Programme (NDBP) is yet to be achieved.  The Committee further observes that the up-
gradation of existing tide gauge network both in terms of software and sensors redeployment of existing current meter and
 deployment of new current meter array along the equator would take place during this financial year. Similarly, the
 Committee would appreciate if under the programme Ocean Dynamics and Modeling (INDOMOD), validation of Coupled

file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/85th.html[29-08-2018 16:17:22]
 Atmospheric Ocean Model (CAOM) to provide forcing parameter for ocean general circulation model and sensitivity test for
 CAOM for prediction of storm surges associated with tropical cyclone along the Indian coast would be conducted and
 validated.  The experiments to determine the sensitivity for development of hybrid coupled model for prediction of Indian
 monsoon regions have also to be achieved.
(Para 51)
 
Action Taken by the Department
      In the period from August 97-Feb.99, all the 12 data buoys as envisaged were developed.  Some of the buoys were frequently
 damaged or vandalized. However, during the last three years operation period of NDBP, the maintenance of data buoys have been
 regularly carried out by the engineers and technicians of NIOT. Proposal for indigenisation of data buoy production and management
 within India to meet the future requirements is being formulated for necessary approval of Government. 
      During the 9
th Plan period DOD formulated a programme on Indian Ocean Modelling (INDOMOD)with the objective to develop
 ocean state forecast  of the Indian Seas.  IISC, Bangalore, IIT, Delhi, CMMACS, Bangalore, IITM, Pune, NIO, Goa and Cochin
 University are undertaking programmes  to develop the numerical model and necessary infrastructure to achieve goal.  During the last
 3-4 years significant progress has been made in the improvements to the prediction of storm surge, development of model for real time
 forecast of Oceanic conditions and prediction of spatial distribution of SST, current and biological productivity etc.
Comments
      While the Committee appreciates the Department’s efforts for undertaking programmes aimed at developing Ocean  Observation
 Information Service for different States. The Committee is of the view that the data collected must be timely disseminated so that the
 same can be utilised to predict cyclones and prevent loss of  life and property.
Coastal Community Programmes
Recommendation
      The Committee recommends that the Department should develop the shore to vessel communication system and commission the
 system in A&N and Lakshdweep Islands which would be helpful for fishermen going for fishing in high seas.  The technology should
 be handed over to the State Governments for continuous operation and maintenance.
(Para 53)
Action Taken by the Department
      The Department has assigned the task of completion and commissioning of the Shore to Fishing Vessel Communication System in
 Pondicherry, Saligao in Goa and Andaman and Nicobar Islands, to NIOT.  SAMEER, a unit of Department of Electronics which was
 involved in identification of sites and the field testing of the Shore to Fishing Vessel Communication System, is being involved in
 testing the commissioned units in West Bengal and Orissa.  Imparting training to the Fisheries Department staff and installation of the
 tower and the system in three sites, one each in Pondicherry, Goa and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.  Since there is lack of response
 from Lakshadweep Administration on installation of the System and also due to the logistics problems involved in transportation of
 the base station equipment, tower, etc., Lakshadweep site has been deleted from the purview of the programme.  It may also be noted
 that Fishermen of Lakshadweep Island go to sea mainly for tuna fishing using pole and line as the prime fishing method and they are
 less vulnerable as compared to the  fishermen in the East Coast who always face the risk of high velocity winds, cyclones, etc.
The technology will be handed over to the State/UT Governments concerned for continuous operation and maintenance as soon as
 the systems become operational .
Comments
      The Committee notes the position.
Island Development
Recommendation
      The Committee shares the perception that the genetic and biotic equilibrium should be maintained in the Indian
 environment.  However, it is of the view that the Department should carry out further research on formulation of appropriate
 feeds for maximum growth of lobsters and also develop the larval rearing technology in Indian spiny lobster.  At the same
 time the Department should also implement projects on development of technology for sustainable shrimp farming, lobster
 and seaweed culture and polyculture of marine organisms at Andaman & Nicobar Centre for Ocean Science & Technology.
(Para No. 60)
Action Taken by the Department
      “Ocean Science and Technology for Islands” focuses on developing sustainable technologies for breeding, rearing, sea ranching
 and fattening/culture of marine organisms such as lobsters, crabs, and other fin and shell fish of commercial importance.  The
 enhancement of marine living resources programme under this project, to begin with, is focusing on developing the larval rearing

INTRODUCTION 
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests, having
 been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this Eighty-Sixth Report of the Committee.  This Report
 deals with  the detailed Demands for Grants (2001-2002) of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (Ministry of Science
 and Technology) (Demand No.69).
 
2.         In the meeting of the Committee held on the 29 th  March, 2001 the Secretary and other Officers of the Department of Scientific and
 Industrial Research gave an overview of the various activities of the Department and the Members sought clarifications on various aspects of the
 performance of the Department to enable it to scrutinise the Demands for Grants.
3.     The Committee expresses its thanks to the Officers of the Department for replying to the clarifications sought by the Members and
 placing before it the required material to enable the Committee to scrutinise the Demands for Grants of the Department of Scientific and
 Industrial Research. 
4.         The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on  9th April, 2001. 
New Delhi;                                                                                                    C. RAMACHANDRAIAH,
April 9,2001                                                                                                                    Chairman,
                            Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests. 
 
R E P O R T
  
The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) which forms part of the Ministry of Science & Technology is entrusted with the
 task of undertaking activities/programmes in respect of Council of Scientific and Industrial Research; Schemes in specific areas of Scientific and
 Industrial Research such as Research and Development by Industry (RDI), Programme Aimed at Technological Self Reliance (PATSER), Scheme
 to Enhance the Efficacy of Transfer of Technology (SEETOT), National Information System for Science and Technology (NISSAT) and support
 to international scientific institutions such as Asian and Pacific Centre for Transfer of Technology, New Delhi; and two public sector enterprises
 viz. National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) and Central Electronics Limited(CEL).
2.   The thrust of the DSIR programmes and activities are centered around promoting industrial R&D; development and
 commercialisation of technologies; acquisition, management and export of technologies and consultancy capabilities; and supporting
 development of information systems on S&T.   
3.   The CSIR is the national R&D organisation providing scientific & industrial research for India’s economic growth and human
 welfare. It has a country wide network of forty laboratories and eighty field centres covering fundamental and applied R&D in all areas
 of science and technology barring atomic research, developing and nurturing S&T human resource for the country  through awards,

86th
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20S%20and%20T,%20Env.%20and%20Forests/86th.html[29-08-2018 16:17:22]
 fellowships etc.   Its range of activities cover practically the entire spectrum of industrial R&D ranging from aerospace to mining to
 microelectronics  to  metallurgy and so on.  CSIR was also assigned the responsibility to coordinate and manage the activities relating to
 a new prestigious and challenging scheme, New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership, initiated in 2000 with the objective to 
 secure for India a global leadership position based on technology.  Some of the thrust areas under the consideration of CSIR are
 catalysing civilian aircraft industry, greening of leather industry, new drug discovery through symbiosis of biodiversity, heritage of
 therapeutic knowledge and modern S&T, enhancing hydrocarbons resource base, gas hydrates, promoting National IPR movement,
 spearheading global technology leadership by industry, pioneering knowledge based exports, nurturing budding talent for science.  CSIR
 derives its finances   from  three  major  sources  namely , i)  Budgetary  support  from the Government under plan and non-plan, ii)
 Undertaking of contract R&D, consultancy & Technical services, and iii) Internal receipts.
4.   Some of the notable achievements of CSIR are, operationalisation of the New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative
 (NMITLI); bringing relief to Cyclone affected people of Orissa by providing them drinking water; efforts of Central Institute of
 Medicinal &Aromatic Plants(CIMAP), Lucknow in making India top in Mint Oil production in the world; maximising blast furnace
 productivity; and organisation of 1999  R&D Management Conference with a theme- R&D as a business.

 970.38 crores in the B.E. and Rs. 910.61 crores in the R.E. of 2000-2001.

6.   The details of the budgetary projections for the programmes of the DSIR during the year 2001-2002 is given at Annexure-I.
7.   The allocation on the plan side has been kept at Rs. 360.00 crores, which represents an increase of about Rs. 32.52 crores over the
 R.E. and about Rs. 5.00 crores over the B.E. of  2001-2002.
8.   The Committee has been informed that over 80% of the Non-Plan expenditure of CSIR goes to meet the committed liabilities on salaries,
 pension and related expenditure of scientists and support staff, on support to nurture human resources for R&D, and remaining 20% for
 contingencies, maintenance of laboratories & residential complexes.  Thus the Non-Plan expenditure has been kept at the barest minimum
 possible.  The laboratories are making all efforts to generate External-Cash-Flow (ECF) to supplement the overall budgetary grant.  The External-
Cash-Flow in 1999-2000 was around Rs.250 crore. Since the Indian industry is presently at cross-roads and is not in a position to make long term
 and substantial investments in R&D.  Thus CSIR is not able to greatly enhance its External Cash Flow.
9.   About new programmes in the field of Scientific and Industrial Research in the year under review, the Committee has been informed
 that  the year 2001-2002 is the terminal year of the Ninth Five Year Plan.  Hence, the emphasis has to be on completion of on-going and
 continuing schemes and not on initiating new ones.  Nonetheless a new scheme on New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership
 Initiative (NMITLI) has been initiated in 2000-2001 to support selectively, innovation centered scientific & technological developments
 in niche areas that could attain for the country a global leadership position. 
10.     The Committee commends the steps being taken by the Department in augmenting its scientific and industrial capabilities towards
 the economic and social development of the Country.  The Committee however   recommends  that  besides the on-going research
 projects, the Department should also support employment generating research such as  research on Bamboo from which millions of
 people earn their livelihood world wide. This would help in generating employment among rural people.
11.   The Committee feels that on the one hand efforts should continue to be made for securing more and more research projects and test-
 work from the industry.  At the same time endeavour should continue by reducing work force by not filling vacancies caused by
 resignations, retirement etc.  This would help ensure optimum utilisation of the human resources and bring about some reduction in non-
plan expenditure.
STAFF STRENGTH
12.In response to a specific question about the staff strength and whether any steps have been contemplated in line with Government’s approach to
 suitably reduce the staff, the Committee has been informed that the total staff strength of DSIR in the year 2000-2001 was 87 and in 2001-02, 64
 only.  The corresponding figures in 40 laboratories, 80 field centres and Headquarters of CSIR were 22,000 and 21,000 as against a sanctioned
 staff strength, after 10% cut, of around 25,000.  Thus the CSIR has already made severe reduction in the sanctioned staff strength.  Nonetheless
 the CSIR had appointed a Committee to reassess and refix the staff strength of laboratories and  Headquarters.  The report of the Committee is

 under submission.  It is the endeavour of CSIR to make the organization even more slim and trim and work towards a total staff strength not
 exceeding 20,000 by the end of 10th Five Year Plan.
13.     The Committee conveys its appreciation for the efforts made to bring about reduction in the staff strength.  The Committee hopes
 that the Department would keep its word in reducing the staff strength to 20,000 by the end of 10th plan.
14   A mention has been made in the Notes on Demands for Grants 2001-2002 about the residential buildings, staff quarters and other
 amenities.  The Committee considers it to be an important area with regard to the welfare of the officers and staff of the Ministry/DSIR
 including CSIR and Laboratories.  The Department was therefore asked about the details of the project, including cost and the number of
 quarters/details of amenities sought to be provided and the percentage of satisfaction enjoyed by the staff in this regard.
15.  In reply it was stated by the CSIR that the concern expressed by the Committee for housing and other amenities for the employees
 provided ‘psychic’ satisfaction that helps to attract and retain some talent in CSIR.  The location of laboratories is divided under 3
 categories viz. those in (i) Metro cities (ii) other towns and (iii) remote areas.  The present level of satisfaction and the targets set for
 satisfaction for the three categories are metros: 13% vs 50%; other towns: 46% vs. 70% and remote areas: 57% vs. 80%.  Thus there is
 substantial unsatiated demand.  The major activity in 2000-2001 was improving the housing satisfaction level at the metros at Bangalore,
 Hyderabad and Delhi where inroads of IT sector on human resources  were being felt and in remote areas like Palampur and Karaikudi
 where appropriate talent needs to be attracted and retained.  In 2001-02, the initiatives  would be completed and activities in ‘other
 towns’ like Bhubaneshwar, Dhanbad, Mysore and  Nagpur would be initiated.
16.     The Committee feels that in order to make available best talent it is necessary that at least the minimum needs of employees are
 taken care of in this fast changing world.  It is all the more necessary because the monetary benefits given by the Fifth Pay Commission
 have to a large extent been neutralized by high cost of services and rising costs of living. The employees, be they of Central Government
 or elsewhere are again on subsistence wage level with high component of personal taxation whereas according to Taylor’s concept of
 scientific management, a satisfied worker is an asset to an organisation.  The Committee therefore feels that every possible effort
 including adequate budgetary support should be provided for amenities like housing.
 
NATIONAL LABORATORIES
17.  CSIR     today   has     a    network    of    40   laboratories    and  80  field stations/extension centres/ regional centres located all over
 the country to undertake R&D in various S&T  disciplines such as molecular biology to metallurgy, seismicity to science policy, from
 aerospace to reach the diverse users and disseminate knowledge and information on R&D capabilities, techniques and technologies
 developed by the National Laboratories of CSIR. The synergy of CSIR’s competence is sought to be optimized by aligning its R&D
 programme/activities more directly with the socio-economic objectives of the country focusing sharply on areas where investments can
 produce maximum returns for CSIR and the country.
18.While the Committee is aware that the year 2001-2002 being the terminal year of the Ninth Five Year Plan, the emphasis has to be
 given on completion of on-going schemes, the Committee would however like the DSIR to endeavour to bring about diversification in
 R&D work.  While the user services for the industry may continue to be provided, prioritisation and diversification of research may help
 to decrease the dependence on non-plan expenditure.  Efforts should also be made to secure research work from abroad to the extent
 possible.
19.Considering the needto upgrade/replace antiquated and obsolete equipment in realizing  its goals, a scheme on Modernisation of equipment and
 R&D facilities at National laboratories was initiated during the Ninth Five Year Plan.  This labwise modernisation proposals were approved in
 1998-99 and proposed  to be continue in 2001-2002 also.  The equipments and R&D facilities at various laboratories of the CSIR were proposed
 to be  modernized and upgraded in the phased manner which will help in augmenting the  currency and competitiveness of the laboratories.
20.At the same time the Committee is happy to note that in pursuance of its recommendations made earlier for providing adequate budgetary
 support to CSIR for modernisation of its equipment and R&D facilities in the National Laboratories, Government have formulated a separate
 schemes on modernization in the Ninth Five Year Plan (NFYP) and Laboratory-wise modernisation plans were formulated.  The total outlay on
 modernization was Rs.360 crores over NFYP of which Rs.260 crores was budgetary support and Rs.100 crores over was to be met from internal
 receipts.  The selective modernization of equipment and R&D facilities is expected to be completed as per schedule by the end of 2001-2002. 
 However, many of the CSIR laboratories are now five decades old – the laboratory buildings, infrastructure and facilities were built then. 
 Although CSIR has diligently maintained them yet the time has taken its toll, for example the electrical wiring, telephones, laboratory safety
 systems have become obsolete.  These need to be modernized if CSIR is to retain semblance of global competitiveness. 
21.  The Committee clarifies that the modernisation includes all aspects not only with regard to the state-of-the-art machineries etc. for
 testing purposes but also includes interior decoration that is necessary to attract the users by giving the look of a modern office.  It also
 includes repairs or replacement of buildings wherever considered necessary and repair/replacement of electrical fittings, telephones,
 safety systems prevalent in a laboratory.
22.   The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation made in 73 rd report and observes that there is need to progressively modernize
 the CSIR Laboratories.  The Committee observes that the process of modernization should be time bound.  The Department should also
 spell out precisely the areas of modernization being undertaken/proposed to be undertaken in the laboratories.  The Department should
 also ensure that the modernization matches the international  standards.  Also,  the  Committee should be  apprised  about  the

training being imparted/proposed to be imparted to the scientists for handling the upgraded/modernized laboratories.  The Committee,

NATIONAL S&T HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT
23.  CSIR has been contributing significantly to the development of highly qualified S&T manpower at the national level.  It had been
 able to create and nurture R&D manpower at all levels, over a wide spectrum of disciplines.  The main objective of extra mural S&T
 HRD programmes is to maintain and continuously upgrade the stock of well qualified, highly specialized scientists, engineers and
 technologists for R&D in all disciplines of science and technology in the country. This objective is sought to be achieved by the CSIR by
 offering Junior and Senior Research Fellowships and Research Associateships tenable in Universities and institutions of higher
 education; supporting symposia/seminars; fostering excellence in research by award of prestigious prizes; and operating the Scientists’
 Pool scheme by offering Senior Research Associateships. Under the programme, the expertise of non-resident Indian scientists and
 technologist is sought to be tapped for the benefit of the country through Transfer of Knowledge/know-how Through Expatriate
 Nationals (TOKTEN) scheme and Interface with NON-Resident Indian Scientists and Technologists programme (INRIST).
24.CSIR would continue to support external research through grants to researchers in Universities as it has helped in improving the scientific and
 engineering research in the country and has greatly contributed to spawning of new specialised schools.
25.The Committee has been informed that in order to maintain tempo of scientific research activities  the scheme of Junior Research Fellowship
 and Senior research Fellowship were monitored and reviewed by an extramural, interdepartmental expert Committee chaired by the Director
 General, CSIR.  Moreover, a new scheme “Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Fellowship” has been introduced with a view to support creative and
 innovativeness at the post-graduate level.
26.The Committee observes that the Universities and Institutions will have to play a meaningful role to achieve widespread excellence in
 both teaching quality and high calibre human resources. Therefore, there is a need for reviewing and strengthening/revamping the
 existing S&T support systems in the universities and other educational institutions, be it in terms of infrastructure or quantum of funding
 as well as operational structures and mechanisms. The issues related to the institutional mechanisms, policy guidelines, approval and
 clearance of procedures should be looked into with a view to simplify and make them user friendly.
27.   The Committee feels that CSIR should also consider introducing Scientific Research Scholarships to school leaving students in order
 to encourage them to pursue a career in S&T related areas. National Women Scientific Research Award could also be introduced to the
 outstanding women researchers to encourage their partnership in the mainstream. These initiatives would help in accelerating the pace of
 scientific & technological research for the development of a strong knowledge base and its application for the welfare of humankind.
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY 
28.  CSIR’s Intellectual Property(IP) policy seeks to maximise the benefits to CSIR from its intellectual capital by stimulating higher
 levels of innovation through a judicious system of rewards, ensuring timely and effective legal protection for its IP and forging strategic
 alliances for enhancing the value of its IP.  CSIR has set for itself a formidable goal holding a valuable portfolio of at least 1000 Indian
 patents and 500 foreign patents by 2001 so that it can use this as the basis of forging strategic alliances with some of the global
 technological leaders in specific areas and generate at least 1% of its R&D budget from IP licensing/alliances.  CSIR would also
 endeavour to be a national resource and an international reference centre on IP matters. Major programmes under IPR include
 comprehensive protection of intellectual property generated and safeguarding against infringement and patent information services.
29.   The Committee commends the efforts made by the CSIR in maintaining its standards for Intellectual Property Movement by setting
 a formidable goal of achieving 1000 Patents and 500 foreign Patents by 2001. The Committee, however, feels that the Department should
 create a Patent Facilitating Cell which should assist in writing, and completing of all formalities for filing of patents. Roving seminars
 should also be conducted at regular intervals to create awareness on intellectual property rights and related issues.
TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT
30.On the Technology Management front, CSIR negotiated and tied  up marketing of technologies with various Indian and Foreign companies and 
 continue to endeavour to catalyse management of technology in the country. The manipulation of technology management as a part of CSIR’s
 strategy is being attempted through alliances and external IPR acquisitions/barter. This would need investments in accessing commercially
 valuable information and data globally thus enhancing acquisition of skills and  competence of the employees. In order to promote in-house and
 national management of technology CSIR organized the prestigious 1999 R&D Management Conference with the theme R&D as Business, in
 association with the famous R&D Management Association U.K.  This has helped to promote a forum for discussing and finding solutions in the
 field of Management of Technology not only in the CSIR but also externally as well.
NEW MILLENNIUM INDIAN TECHNOLOGY LEADERSHIP (NMITLI)
31.  New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative (NMITLI) scheme was launched in 2000  in order to  support innovation
 centered scientific and technological developments as a vehicle to attain a global leadership position in some selected niche areas for the
 country.  It would be based on partnership between the government and private sector.  Appropriate mechanism for accomplishing this
 initiative would be evolved by CSIR.
32.When asked to explain as to how at the last year RE stage the allocation was reduced to half of the total amount i.e. Rs.25 crores, the Secretary
 informed the Committee that after wide-ranging and wide-spread national consultations through letters, media, brainstorming meeting and posters,
 28 potential areas have been short listed and groups were set-up for preparing detailed project      proposals    at   national   level    for   12   of   
 the   areas   in   the   first    phase.    The projects were then subjected to techno-economic evaluation by   High Powered  Committee  (HPC)  and
 the recommendations of  the HPC  were subsequently considered by the Governing Body of CSIR.  Nine projects at a total cost of about Rs.54.00
 crores were approved with the first year’s outlay of around Rs.35.00 crore.  He, however, assured the Committee that during this financial year no

33.The Committee notes with satisfaction that a beginning towards technology leadership has been made in NMITLI. However, it is
 constrained to observe that there has been poor projection of the programme and the financial visualization has been unsatisfactory;

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT BY INDUSTRY (RDI)
34.Recognising the need for developing an indigenous technological base for technology absorption and indigenous technology development for
 achieving technological self reliance, the Government has initiated several measures to encourage industry, carry out R&D in order to enable it to
 meet its requirements and  also  for establishing close links between the national laboratory system   and industry. The scheme deals with all the
 activities relating to recognition of in-house R&D industrial units and non-commercial Scientific and Industrial Research Organisations, fiscal
 incentives and other mechanisms and initiatives towards supporting and encouraging the R&D initiatives of industry.  In-house R&D units in
 industry provide a desirable and essential interface between efforts within the national laboratories and the educational sector as well as
 production in industry.  At present there are around 1160 in-house R&D units duly recognised by DSIR.  They employ over 50,000 R&D
 personnel. The R&D expenditure incurred by these units was around Rs.2000 crores in 1999-2000.  The objective of the scheme is to sharply
 focus on R&D by Industry and to strengthen linkages among in-house R&D system, National Laboratory System and educational system and
 strengthen R&D infrastructure in industry and promote and support R&D initiatives of the industry.
35.The Committee observes that the socio-economic advancement of a nation demands a strong relationship between Industry and R&D
 laboratories, which unfortunately is not a reality in India. Rather the wholesome involvement of national R&D with industry, which is a
 hallmark of the advanced industrial societies, is missing in India. The Committee, therefore, recommends that CSIR laboratories should
 put more emphasis on consolidating its partnership with the Industry so that the technologies developed by the laboratories can be
 commercialized and fully exploited. More the commercialization of technologies, more would be the confidence in the CSIR
 laboratories, providing further impetus  to their R&D activities.
NATIONAL INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY (NISSAT)
36.The NISSAT programme was initiated in 1977 to envisage promotion and support to the development of a compatible set of information
 systems for science & technology and interlinking these into a network. Its objectives include development of national information services,
 promotion of existing information systems & services, introduction of modern information handling tools & techniques, promotion of
 international cooperation in information, development of indigenous products & services, organization of skill development programmes and
 promotion of R&D in information science & technology. 
37.  In order to promote the development of indigenous products and services and promote national information services, NISSAT has established
 sectoral centres in the areas of leather technology, food technology, machine tools production and engineering, drugs and pharmaceuticals, textiles
 & allied subjects, chemicals & allied industries, management sciences, marine and aquatic sciences.   These centres provide bibliographic as well
 as factual and numeric information to meet various information   needs of academicians, scientists, technologists, entrepreneurs, management
 executives and decision-makers.  The centres are usually built around the existing information sources and facilities.  They maintain extensive
 collection of published and unpublished documents in  the form of books, periodicals, R&D reports, technical reports, standards, patents and trade
 literature in their subject areas. NISSAT has also created a CD-ROM National Collection Centre.  This centre collects products,  documents nation
 wide on CD-ROM.  The Centre also provides services from  this information.
38.NISSAT has two effective media - a quarterly publication, Information Today & Tomorrow (ITT), that acts as an industry – technology watch,
 and (ii) the annual meet on ITT which brings the industry-promoter-service provider-and more importantly the user on a common platform. 
 Besides, most of the NISSAT supported Centres bring out their own publications and databases and leave their websites and web servers to
 provide global access to their services and products.  In addition, representatives  of similar organizations and user institutions are involved in
 various national level/local level committees not only to benefit from their inputs, but also check avoidable duplication.
39.The Committee was informed that in the current year, the Department intended to cover under the programme,  the activities such as
 establishment of a Virtual Information Centre at ICICI  at Hyderabad and an internet Portal on Knowledge Management; emphasis  on web-based
 information content development in their information centers; development of an Indian S&T web server covering a variety of Indian S&T
 information; development of indigenous database activities; and implementation of National Plan of action on Scientometrics  and Biblometrics
 and conduct a series of R&D studies etc.
40.The Committee is of the view that dissemination of  information can be facilitated  through electronic network,  as well as physical
 networks like libraries, booksellers, broadcasting companies and organizations selling information in electronic form e.g. database
 available in the form of CD-ROM, DVD etc. Widespread dissemination of information depends upon availability of reliable and
 dependable networks.  Therefore, The Department should try to create appropriate delivery mechanisms.  Such delivery mechanisms
 would provide quality education, create a strong knowledge base and provide widespread access to information to the research
 community as well. 
PROGRAMME AIMED AT TECHNOLOGICAL SELF-RELIANCE (PATSER)
41.The  Programme Aimed at Technological Self-Reliance  (PATSER) aims at catalyzing and supporting activities relating to technology
 absorption, adaptation and demonstration including capital goods development, involving industry and R&D organizations. The main objective of
 the Programme is to support industry for technological development, demonstration and absorption of imported technology; build indigenous
 capabilities for development and commercialization of contemporary  products and processes of high impact; involving national research
 organizations in joint projects with industry; and technology evaluation in selected sectors/areas. The Department’s support to the projects has
 been catalytic providing impetus to the R&D efforts of industry,  though   bulk  of the financial  input  for  the projects  comes  from  the  industry

 Generally, DSIR meets 30-40% of the total project cost and the remaining expenditure is met by the Industry.  DSIR has supported over 110
 projects so far, involving  a total project cost of Rs.158 crores with its share of Rs.47 crores   i.e.  around 30%.
42.A distinctive feature of  PATSER  funding is that many of the programmes also involve Govt. research laboratories or IITs, IISc, or
 Universities as partners along with the industrial companies. Further, in order to nurture and promote  technopreneural skills  of Indian citizens  
 at   individual   level,    projects    are    supported   under a scheme viz. “ Technopreneur Promotion Programme (TePP)”, jointly operated by
 DSIR under the PATSER scheme and Department of Science & Technology under the “ Home Grown Technology” scheme.   The
 Technopreneur  Promotion Programme aims to provide financial support to individual innovators having original ideas and helps them convert
 these into working models. So far, over 30 projects have been supported under TePP. 
43.The PATSER scheme has proved  successful in synergising  the R&D efforts of industry and national research organizations. The Committee
 has been  informed that under PATSER scheme, 6 new projects for technology development and demonstration have been approved and 14 more
 were expected to be approved by March, 2001. 75 on-going projects were being monitored for progress  and some of the PATSER projects were
 in an advanced stage of development. Besides, 5 Patents have been filed  or were in the process of being filed or scaled up during 2000-2001.
44.The Committee further been informed that  about 25 new projects and  85 on-going projects for technology development and demonstration
 were planned to be supported during 2001-2002.  Besides, by  inviting fresh proposals from industry, DSIR would proactively interact with other
 ministries for identification of new products/processes required and promote technology development projects with small and medium
 enterprises.  Besides supporting the projects, DSIR would organize/support more interactions of industry, research organizations and concerned
 agencies for identifying future trends and needs for new/improved technologies.
45.The Committee notes with satisfaction the support rendered by the DSIR in the field of technology absorption and adaptation. The
 Department should continue its efforts to interact with other Ministries for wider dissemination and utilization of its technology
 development projects.  This would help in generating new technologies.  An integrated and sustained approach would certainly help the
 Department in realizing its projected goals.  Besides, it is necessary to create awareness about the Technopreneur Promotion Programme
 (TePP) so that enthused and encouraged individual innovators come out with their  creative talents.
 SCHEME TO ENHANCE THE EFFICACY OF TRANSFER OF TECHNOLOGY (SEETOT)
46.The SEETOT aims to facilitate acquisition and management of technologies, accelerate export of technologies and services, enhance the
 consultancy capabilities of the Department and increase awareness about the usefulness of consultancy services among the customers. Under the
 scheme, development and commercialization of indigenous technologies is encouraged and international organizations concerned with technology
 transfer, such as Asian and Pacific Centre for Transfer of Technology, are supported.
47.  The main objectives of the scheme are to provide technical and technological inputs for acquisition and management of technologies;
 accelerate technology intensive exports; enhance consultancy capabilities; and  support mechanisms for  technology transfer, facilitate 
 preparation
of reports, newsletters, organisation of seminars and participation in trade fairs related to promotion of technology exports.
48.   The Committee is of the view that the need for transfer of technology   in bringing improvement in industrial productivity can not be
 underestimated. The Committee is pained to observe that Transfer of Technology programmes have moved at snail’s pace.  It is
 necessary to  identify the  prevailing constraints and have insight of Industrial sector problems and then devise appropriate technologies
 to address the problems.  To that end, the Committee recommends that a multi-disciplinary team should work on priority basis for
 identification and solution of the problems being faced with regard to the technology.
49.The Committee would also like to point out that  it is equally necessary to plan the research projects beforehand, concentrate and
 conduct research only in those areas where it can gainfully be employed in the interest of the economy.    The Committee, therefore, feels
 that the scientists and all others working  for transfer of technology should bear in mind all these points
ECOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENT
50.Central Fuel Research Institute(CFRI) Dhanbad has developed energy efficient, environment friendly and low cost coke ovens to produce soft
 coke that dispense with the conventional burning of coal in open atmosphere. CFRI had also developed fly ash soil amendment technology which
 has been extensively demonstrated through field trials with varying proportions of fly ash under different agroclimatic conditions and soil types in
 different types in different parts of the country for cultivation of various cereals, root, leguminous and vegetable crops.  A substantial increase in
 crop yield, early maturity of crops and improvement in physio-chemical properties of  the soil without any adverse effect are the advantages of
 this technology.
51.Regional Research Laboratory, Bhubaneshwar has developed a new method to utilise lignin, a pulp and paper mills waste to produce phenol
 formaldehyde resin powder, used as raw material for making bakelite plastic and vanillin used in cakes and the ice-cream industry. Central
 Building Research Institute, Roorkee has also developed clay flyash bricks through de-airing extrusion and stabilized lime flyash bricks through
 vibro-compaction.
FOOD AND FOOD PROCESSING
52.CSIR is playing a vital role in Food Processing sector.  The R&D programmes being pursued by the Council are related to development of pre
 and post harvest technologies for wide range of fruit with an objective to minimize wastage and increase the shelf life of the produce with
 desirable and acceptable ripening characteristics.
53.The food processing is primarily done to improve and safeguard the agricultural productivity reducing wastage of perishable food items like

 during the session when the crop for those products does not  grow.
54.  Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysore in collaboration with the Coconut Development Board (CDB) have
 developed a low cost simple processing technology for the production of Coconut Vinegar used as food preservative and flavouring
 agent from matured coconut water using vinegar generators. CFTRI has also developed two nutrient enriched snacks namely  ‘nitro
 biscuits’ and ‘suruchi meetha’ both valuable as items for the mid-day meal schemes in schools. The laboratory has also developed an
 inexpensive, pilot maize mill with I ton/hour capacity  for dry milling  of maize under the  Technology Mission for Oil seeds,  pulses
and maize. Regional Research Laboratory, Trivendrum, has developed a process for extraction of ginger oil directly from fresh ginger.
55.   The Committee  visited  CFTRI, Mysore a few years back and had the occasion to see some of the machines like large scale dosa
 making machine.  The Committee doubts whether there is demand for machines designed to cater large scale commercial requirement. 
 The Committee would therefore like to impress on all concerned to engage themselves in activities which are either against confirmed
 orders or can otherwise be gainfully exploited.
56.   The Committee feels that in order to provide impetus to the technologies developed by the CSIR laboratories in food processing
 sector, the Department should take the initiative of interacting  with all State Governments for providing sales and trade tax exemption,
 so that interest of the Industry can be sustained in extending the benefit of technologies to the larger sections of the society.
57.   The Committee  suggests that the Department should emphasise on need based R&D activities for cereals, pulses and oilseeds to
 develop marketable products and technology achieving highest recovery and top quality of the desired constituents/parts of the raw
 materials processed with minimum energy spent and no pollution created.
58.   The Committee holds a view that besides food processing technologies, the Department should also augment Post Harvest Technology
 (PHT). The technology so developed must lead to rural industrialization and thereby create employment and income generation
 opportunities. Appropriate PHT would help in enhancing per capita food and fibre availability from the limited and dwindling land and
 water resources.
SPECIAL PACKAGE FOR NORTH-EAST
59.In order to develop North Eastern region of the country, Government have adopted a special approach.  Government have therefore sought to
 give a special package to North Eastern among others, to facilitate their assimilation as also their participation in  the mainstream of National life. 
 Asked whether this has been reflected in the programmes and activities of the Department, the Committee was informed that the Department of
 Scientific & Industrial Research and the CSIR laboratories have accorded due importance to providing R&D of value and S&T outputs for the
 effective utilization of endogenous resources of the NE Region (NER).  CSIR has a full fledged Regional Research laboratory at Jorhat along with
 a branch laboratory at Itanagar and field station at Imphal which provides dedicated S&T inputs for economic & industrial development of NER.
 CSIR was implementing specific projects for the development of NER for example (i) pilot project at Assam Oil Division Refinery of Indian Oil
 Corporation at Digboi for developing a short path distillation technology for making value added products i.e. micro-crystalline waxes and quality
 bitumen from vacuum residues – a waste from the refinery, (ii) DSIR/CSIR have provided technology & finance to establish a pilot plant for
 making fresh ginger oil and spice processing at Manipur; (iii) the light transport aircraft being developed at National Aerospace Laboratories,
 Bangalore  will be of immense value to interlinking the NER to the mainland and within the region.  Besides CSIR has taken up seismic
 monitoring and seismic hazards map preparation, bio-propspection, development of agro-technology and  processing technologies for medicinal
 and aromatic plants, coal assessment and utilization, site specific architectural designs for low cost houses etc. for NER.  Several manpower
 development programmes have been organized by DSIR
& CSIR on diverse S&T based knowledge and skills.  Besides, surveys have been conducted to utilize the latent human & natural resources of
 NER.  Thus DSIR & CSIR were committed to provide S&T inputs for development of North-East Region.  It may be noted that along with other
 scientific departments/agencies, DSIR/CSIR have now (from 2001-2002) been exempted from the mandatory requirement  of earmarking 10% of
 the Budget for the NER & Sikkim.  Thus the allocation of resources for NER has not been indicated separately in the Demands for Grants.
PUBLIC SECTOR ENTERPRISES
60.  There are two public sector enterprises, namely, National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) and Central Electronics
 Limited (CEL) under the Department of Scientific & Industrial Research.
61.National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) is engaged in development, upscaling, licensing and commercialisation of indigenous
 technologies as well as export of technologies. The objectives of the Corporation are to commercialise  indigenous technologies; promote 
 commercialisation of inventions; disseminate  information on technology transfer; and facilitate development and promotion of rural technology.
 Some of the achievements of the Corporation in the year 2000-01 include participation in the equity of M/s Twenty First Century Battery Ltd.;
 Development of Interactive Multimedia Training Package on intellectual Property Rights, submission of a proposal to UNDICO  for setting up a
 training centre on the processing of precious stones in Kalahandi and Bolangir districts of Orissa, signing up an agreement  with the Social Fund
 for Development, Govt. of Egypt for setting up of two Science & Technology Entrepreneurship Parks at different  locations in Egypt, etc.  The
 NRDC has been constantly making profits for over 15 years and its MoU performance in 1999-2000 was excellent registering a gross profit of Rs.
 51.97 lakhs as compared to Rs. 45.96 lakhs in 1998-99.
62.   As regards the performance of National Research Development Corporation (NRDC), the Committee is constrained to observe that
 the meagre gross profit earned is in fact a cover for the losses suffered by the unit.  The Committee therefore, recommends that DSIR
 should periodically review the projects/proposals undertaken by the NRDC and make every effort to bring it out of the red for there is no
 case for survival of such units in fast changing times.

 emphasis on indigenous technology, inducted both from its in-house developments and from the country’s national laboratories for its

1.   The Committee commends the steps being taken by the Department in augmenting its scientific and industrial capabilities towards the
 economic and social development of the Country.  The Committee however   recommends  that  besides the on-going research projects,
 the Department should also support employment generating research such as  research on Bamboo from which millions of people earn
 their livelihood world wide. This would help in generating employment among rural people.
(Para 10)

 work from the industry.  At the same time endeavour should continue by reducing work force by not filling vacancies caused by
 resignations, retirement etc.  This would help ensure optimum utilisation of the human resources and bring about some reduction in non-
plan expenditure.
(Para 11)

 elsewhere are against on subsistence wage level with high component of personal taxation whereas according to Taylor’s concept of

Ql.(a)   The total financial outlay for the Department of Scientific & Industrial Research for the year 2001-2002 is Rs. 963.47 crores as
 against Rs. 970.38 crores at B.E. stage and Rs. 910.61 at R.E. stage. While the overall budgetary support has marginally declined in
 comparison to the B.E. last year, the fact remains that the non-plan expend all through remained, more or less, double of plan
 expenditure. What are the reasons and have any steps been contemplated to reduce it? As in the case of National Laboratories too, the
 non-plan expenditure has been more than double of the Plan expenditure whereas in terms of Committee's earlier recommendations, the
 laboratories are expected to generate funds for themselves? What are the reasons for this trend of expenditure in CSIR laboratories?
(b)    Is there any system in the Department to monitor and review the productivity of its ongoing schemes as also the unproductive non-
plan expenditure before formulating proposals for the budgetary support? If so, please furnish Details.
Ans.1(a)The total financial outlay during 2001-02 is Rs. 963.47 crore which consists of Rs.932.22 crore for CSIR and Rs. 31.25 crore for
 DSIR and its PSES. Of the Rs.932.22 crore for CSIR the Plan outlay is Rs. 332 crore and the Non-Plan is Rs.600.22 crore.
(Rs. In Crore)
YEAR                                       Budget Allocation                         Ratio of  Expenditure 
    PLAN      NON PLAN     TOTAL      PLAN    NON PLAN
1998-99                       204.00            509.32         713.32             29          71
1999-2000                     250.00            543.24         793.24             32          68

 2001-02 ( B.E.)              332.00            600.22         932.22            36          64
It will be seen that as a % of the total expenditure the Non Plan component has declined over the past three years. Further over 80% of the
 Non-Plan expenditure of CSIR goes to meet the committed liabilities on salaries, pension and related expenditure of scientists and
 support staff, on support to nurture human resources for R&D, and only 20% for contingencies, maintenance of laboratories & residential
 complexes. Thus the Non-Plan expenditure has been kept at the barest minimum possible. The laboratories are making all efforts to
 generate external-cash-flow, (ECF) to supplement the overall budgetary grant. The external-cash-flow in 1999-2000 was around Rs. 250
 crore. The Indian industry is presently at cross-roads and is not in a position to make long term and substantial investments in R&D.
 Thus CSIR is not able to greatly enhance its ECF. But for the undertaking of externally funded projects and supplementation of resources
 from ECF the CSIR scientists would not have been able to achieve and deliver the desired performance outputs and targets.
 
(b) The Department has a well structured system of monitoring the programme/projects/activities for its various schemes. Every scheme
 has a specialised Committee to monitor and advise on the overall performance of the scheme and expert/technical group to examine in
 detail the specific projects and programmes. In the CSIR the S&T programmes are monitored at three levels: (i) the Research Councils of
 the respective laboratories; (ii) Review at the Director-General's/HQ. level and (iii) for the major and important programmes by
 Governing Body of OSIR.
Q2. In the recent past there have been many Parliament Questions arising out of CAG's reports (e.g. 5 of 2000) on expenditure incurred in
 some of the institutions and laboratories under the CSIR on telephones, foreign visits and such other heads? Have you looked into the
 frivolity or otherwise of such expenditure. If so, with what results?
Ans.     In the C& AG report referred to test check of 14 CSIR laboratories was undertaken and the observations were that few of the
 laboratories had incurred irregular expenditure on hospitality, telephones etc. The irregular expenditure commented upon was only of the
 order of Rs. 38 lakhs out of RsIO,000 lakh of expenditure test checked. The matter of tightening even this minimal misapplication of
 expenditure was examined by a high level committee. Revised stringent instructions/guidelines have been issued thereon with a system
 of checks and balances to ensure transparency and accountability. A Committee has since been constituted to enquire into specific cases
 of expenditure as pointed out by CAG.
Q3.    What is the present staff strength as also in last 2 years of the Ministry of S&T, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research,
 CSIR including the laboratories? Whether any step is contemplated in line with Government's approach to suitably reduce the staff? If
 so, the details thereof?
Ans.   The total staff strength of DSIR in the year 2000-2001 was 87 and in 2001- 2002 64 only. In the 40 laboratories, 80 field centres and Hqrs of
 CSIR the corresponding figures were 22,000 and 21000 as against a sanctioned staff strength, after 10% cut, of around 25,000. Thus the CSIR has
 already made severe reduction in the sanctioned staff strength. Nonetheless the CSIR had appointed a committee to reassess and refix the staff
 strength of laboratories & Hqrs. The report of the committee is under submission. It is the endeavour of CSIR to make the organization even more
 slim & trim and work towards a total staff strength not exceeding 20,000 by the end of 10th Five Year Plan.
Q4.   What are the new areas proposed to be covered in the field of Scientific and Industrial Research in the year under review? What has
 been the basis of selecting these areas?
Ans    The year 2001-2002 is the terminal year of the Ninth Five Year Plan. As per the prevailing guidelines the emphasis has to be on
 completion of on-going and continuing schemes and not on initiating new ones. Nonetheless a new scheme on New Millennium Indian

Q6.    Whether any review of the Programmes Research Schemes, Scholarships & Fellowship, for which Rs. 56.50 crores has been kept in 2001-
2002, been undertaken. If so, with what results?
Ans.  There are nine subject wise Committees that continuously monitor and review the programmes of research schemes and suggest any

Q7.  Time and again the Committee has emphasized the modernization of CSIR Laboratories with state of the art facilities designed to cater to the
 needs of the users. It appears that the first step of three-tier hardware infrastructure envisaged in terms of LAN at the Headquarters and the
 laboratories has been accomplished. The initiative to set up MIS is in hand and as first step Is personal based MIS' has been set up across CSIR
 and for "Project" in few labs on a trial basis. The Committee would like to have the. details of the project, salient features, cost and the purpose
 likely to be achieved through the project, for its information.
Ans.   The objectives of the MIS Project are to systematically collect & update organizational data on (i) Human Resources in CSIR and (ii)
 Project Monitoring. The project monitoring system will include all the essentials of the project at the approval stage with predefined financial,
 physical, infrastructural, S&T human resource milestones & targets and their periodic progress & achievement. The activity is presently at the
 level of field testing in a few laboratories and after its feedback and successful validation it would be taken up for adoption across the

Q8.   The Government has sought to give a special package to NE for a variety of reasons, among others, to increase their assimilation as also their
 participation in the main stream of National life. This does not appear to have been reflected in the programmes and activities of your
 Department? If so, the reasons therefore?
Ans. The Department of Scientific & Industrial Research and the CSIR laboratories have accorded due importance to providing R&D of value and
 S&T outputs for the effective utilisation of endogenous resources of the NE Region (NER). CSIR has a full fledged Regional Research Laboratory
 (RRL) at Jorhat along with a branch laboratory at ltanagar and field station at lmphal which provides dedicated S&T inputs for economic &
 industrial development of NER. CSIR is implementing specific projects for the development of NER for example (i) pilot project at Assam Oil
 Division Refinery of Indian Oil Corporation at Digboi for developing a short path distillation technology for making value added products i.e.
 micro-crystalline waxes and quality bitumen from vacuum residues - a waste from the refinery, (ii) DSIR/CSIR have provided technology &
 finance to establish a pilot plant for making fresh ginger oil and spice processing at Manipur; (iii) the light transport aircraft being developed at
 NAL will be of immense value to interlinking the NER  to the  mainland &  within  the region.  Besides  CSIR has taken up seismic  monitoring &
seismic hazards map preparation, bio-propspection, development of agro-technology and processing technologies for medicinal and aromatic
 plants, coal assessment and utilization, site specific architectural designs for low cost houses etc. for NER. Several manpower development
 progammes have been organized by DSIR & CSIR on diverse S&T based knowledge and skills. Besides surveys have been conducted to utilize
 the latent human & natural resources of NER. Thus DSIR & CSIR are committed to provide S&T inputs for development of North-East
 Region.      It may be noted that along with other scientific departments/agencies, DSIR/CSIR have now (from 2001-2002) been exempted from
 the mandatory requirement of earmarking 10% of the Budget for the NER & Sikkim. Thus the allocation of resources for NER has not been
 indicated separately in the demand of grant.
Q9.  It has been stated that the modernization and upgradation of the equipment and R&D facilities was commenced with the budgetary
 support provided in the year 1997-98. The Committee would like to know whether any time schedule was fixed for the completion of
 modernization and upgradation of the facilities in CSIR laboratories: if so, the details thereof and the extent to which the modernisation
 has been achieved?
Ans.  At the outset CSIR would like to convey its gratefulness to the Committee for its recommendations to the Govt. to fund CSIR for
 Modernisation of its equipment and R&D facilities in the National Laboratories. A separate scheme on modernization was initiated in the
 Ninth Five Year Plan (NFYP) and Laboratory-wise, modernisation plans were formulated. The total outlay on modernization was Rs.
 360 crore over NFYP of which Rs. 260 crore was budgetary support and Rs. 100 crore was to be met from internal receipts. The
 selective modernization of equipment & R&D facilities is expected to be completed as per schedule by the end of 2001-2002. However
 many of the CSIR laboratories are now five decades old - the laboratory buildings, infrastructure and facilities were built then. Although
 CSIR has diligently maintained them yet the time has taken its toll; for example the electrical wiring, telephones, laboratory safety
 systems have become obsolete. These need to be modernized if CSIR is to retain semblance of global competitiveness. CSIR would
 request the Committee to consider this aspect of modernization and if found tenable recommend to the Government the modernization of
 its infrastructural facilities in the Tenth Five Year Plan.
